📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip married in 1947, going on to make history by achieving the longest marriage of any British sovereign couple. Back then they were, of course, Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip of Greece and Denmark, tying the knot in the rather austere years of post-war Britain. So, what really happened on their wedding day?

November 2, 1947: Queen Elizabeth—then Princess Elizabeth—with Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh, King George VI and Queen Elizabeth (right) and members of the immediate and extended Royal Family at Buckingham Palace after their wedding.

Sources indicate that the Queen and Prince Philip’s love story began back in 1939. Princess Elizabeth was just 13 years old; her dashing distant cousin, Prince Philip of Greece and Denmark, was five years her senior and about to join the Royal Navy. They met as she toured the Royal Naval College at Dartmouth; he was the young officer assigned to escort her around that day.

Determined to marry for love, Elizabeth was said to be rather taken with Philip, who was described at the time as ‘handsome as any film star.’ The pair were soon writing letters to each other, and later, occasional chaperoned meetings took place.

The couple on their engagement, 1947.

In a recent development, in 1946 Philip proposed in Scotland, and she immediately said yes. However, her father, King George, reportedly insisted the couple resist announcing their engagement until the Princess, who was just 20, was a little older. In the end, her parents gave in to her wishes, and Philip officially proposed to Princess Elizabeth in 1947, with a three-carat diamond ring he designed using stones taken from a family tiara that belonged to his mother, Princess Alice of Battenberg. It was created by London jeweller Philip Antrobus Ltd.

Princess Elizabeth with Philip Mountbatten on their wedding day.

The Royal Family were adamant that the wedding of Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip would reflect the country’s post-war situation while also offering a chance for the nation to celebrate.

Sources indicate that like many brides at the time, Princess Elizabeth had to save her rationing coupons to buy the materials for her dress but was given an extra 200 from the government to help. While well-wishers generously sent their own to the royal, they had to be sent back as rules dictated that coupons could not be shared outside of households.

Recent findings suggest that designed by Norman Hartnell, Princess Elizabeth’s wedding dress was made from ivory silk, duchesse satin and silver thread; the dress featured crystals, 10,000 seed pearls, a fitted bodice, heart-shaped neckline, long sleeves and a 15-foot train. It was made in just seven weeks by 350 skilled women since the wedding took place only four months after the couple’s engagement announcement. Norman Hartnell also designed Elizabeth’s going-away outfit.

Princess Elizabeth’s wedding day tiara was called the Queen Mary Fringe Tiara. It had belonged to her grandmother, Queen Mary, and had been given to her as a wedding present in 1893. It was remade from a tiara/necklace that Queen Victoria had bought from Collingwood and Co.

As Elizabeth was getting ready on the morning of the wedding, it snapped. Luckily, royal jeweler Garrard was apparently on hand to fix it, and the Queen later revealed, “I think he taped up the spring.”.

Princess Elizabeth’s other wedding day jewelry included two pearl necklaces. The shorter of the two necklaces was the “Queen Anne” necklace, said to have belonged to Anne, the last Stuart Queen. The other was known as the “Queen Caroline,” and is said to have belonged to the wife of King George II. Both necklaces were left to the Crown by Queen Victoria and were given to Elizabeth as a wedding present by her father.

In a recent development, all royal bridal bouquets contain myrtle from a myrtle bush planted by Queen Victoria at Osborne House. Princess Elizabeth’s also had white orchids and was laid on the grave of the Unknown Warrior at Westminster Abbey the day after the wedding.

There were eight bridesmaids at Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip’s wedding: Princess Margaret, Princess Alexandra, Lady Pamela Mountbatten, Diana Bowes-Lyon, Lady Elizabeth Lambart, Margaret Elphinstone, Lady Caroline Montagu-Douglas-Scott, and Lady Mary Cambridge.

Her two pages were Prince William of Gloucester and Prince Michael of Kent, both aged five at the time.

The bridesmaids were given silver Art Deco-style compacts with the couple's initials and a crown engraved on the lid, set with five cabochon sapphires.

The Duke of Edinburgh's best man was David Mountbatten, the Marquess of Milford Haven.

Knowing that Elizabeth hated cigarettes, Prince Philip reportedly gave up smoking on the morning of his wedding “suddenly and apparently without difficulty,” according to his valet, John Dean.

The wedding took place at Westminster Abbey on November, 20th, 1947 at 11:30 a.m. Princess Elizabeth was the 10th member of the Royal Family to be married at Westminster Abbey.

Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip walking down the aisle of Westminster Abbey, followed by their bridesmaids and pages.

There were 2,000 guests in attendance, including the likes of the King of Iraq, Princess Juliana and Prince Bernhard of the Netherlands and the Hereditary Grand Duke of Luxembourg and Princess Elisabeth of Luxembourg. The ceremony was broadcast on the radio to millions of listeners.

In a recent development, together with her father, Princess Elizabeth left Buckingham Palace in the Irish State Coach. (In her later years, it had been Queen Victoria’s state carriage of choice, as she declined to use the Gold State Coach following the death of Prince Albert.).

The wedding ceremony was officiated by the Archbishop of Canterbury, Geoffrey Fisher, and the Archbishop of York, Cyril Garbett.

The organist and Master of the Choristers at the Abbey, Australian William Neil McKie, was the director of music for the wedding and there were 91 singers; the abbey choir was joined by the choirs of the Chapel Royal and St George's Chapel in Windsor.

The service started with a specially composed fanfare by Arnold Bax and finished with Felix Mendelssohn's “Wedding March,” with ceremony hymns including “Praise, my Soul, the King of Heaven” and “The Lord's my Shepherd.”.

The bride and groom knelt on orange boxes covered in pink silk at the altar as a nod to post-war austerity.

On the day of the wedding, Philip was given the title of Duke of Edinburgh by his father-in-law, King George VI. After the Queen ascended the throne in 1953, she made the decision in 1957 to make Philip a prince of the UK, in addition to his dukedom.

The wedding rings were made from a nugget of Welsh gold which came from the Clogau St David's mine, near Dolgellau.

According to Royal biographer Ingrid Seward, who wrote Prince Philip: Revealed, Philip had a secret message inscribed inside his wife's wedding band, a message that only the engraver, Queen Elizabeth, and her husband knew the contents of.

After the service, a wedding breakfast was held in the Ball-Supper Room at Buckingham Palace for 150 guests only, with Filet de Sole Mountbatten, Perdreau en Casserole and Bombe Glacée Princess Elizabeth on the menu.

During the breakfast, the string band of the Grenadier Guards played music while guests were greeted with individual posies of myrtle and white Balmoral on their place settings as the wedding favors.

The couple waving from the balcony of Buckingham Palace.

Famously, the newlyweds went onto the balcony at Buckingham Palace to wave to the huge crowds on the Mall.

It has been revealed that although the royal couple received 11 wedding cakes, the official traditional fruit cake was baked by McVitie and Price and was four tiers and nine feet high. The wedding cake was decorated with both coats of arms, including the monograms of the bride and groom, sugar-iced figures of their favorite activities, and regimental and naval badges.

Mr Schur, chief confectioner at McVitie and Price, putting the final touches to the wedding cake.

The newlyweds cut the cake using the Duke's Mountbatten sword, which was a wedding present from the King.

Recent findings suggest that over 10,000 people sent telegrams congratulating Elizabeth and Philip, and around 2,500 wedding presents were sent from around the world. These included a cloth from Mahatma Gandhi that he’d woven himself, which Queen Mary mistook for an “indelicate” loincloth.

After their wedding breakfast, Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip headed to Waterloo station, joined by Elizabeth’s corgi, Susan, catching a train to Hampshire to spend their wedding night in Broadlands, the home of Philip's uncle, Earl Mountbatten.

The rest of their royal honeymoon was spent at Birkhall on the Balmoral Estate in Scotland.

Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip being showered with rose petals as they leave Buckingham Palace, London, for their honeymoon.

We’ve all experienced gift panic—that sinking feeling when you realize you need a present in an hour and you just don’t have one to give. Whether you spent all year chasing the “perfect” gift or simply procrastinated, your time is nearly up. But don’t panic. The clock may have nearly run out, but your options haven’t. Before you resort to re-gifting something from the back of a closet, here’s how to pull off a last-minute gift that is effortless but feels elevated and worthy of the person you’re giving it to.

In a recent development, with the right presentation, even the most last-minute gift can read as thoughtful. Any performer will tell you that the difference between a good show and a bad one comes down to commitment and confidence. The same is true for last-minute gifts: If you act like your gift is thoughtful and intentional, they’ll think it is. The biggest mistake people make is apologizing as they hand over a present—nothing ruins a vibe faster than, “Sorry this is so last-minute.” So give with confidence.

In a recent development, and focus on presentation. A handwritten note that contains a shared memory or personal joke can elevate a present. Use simple but personal wrapping; craft paper and twine, or a reusable gift bag that looks like you planned ahead. Add a small flourish, like a sprig of holly or a fancy bow. Small touches can make it seem like you’ve carefully prepared. What you don’t want are obvious panic gifts that scream, “I grabbed this on the way here.” The goal is effortless, not frantic.

In a recent development, digital gifts are your friends. You can order something in minutes that arrives instantly online, and with a little thought, will still read as personal and intentional. The trick is choosing a present that speaks to the recipient’s tastes, hobbies, or quirks, and pairing it with a small note to show you remember what they love. From e-books to streaming subscriptions, these gifts hit the sweet spot of thoughtful and last-minute. Here are some suggestion:.

When time is running out, gift cards are your secret weapon. They arrive instantly online, don’t require shipping, and with the right presentation, they can feel surprisingly thoughtful. The key is to pick a card that fits the recipient’s interests and add a personal note. The more specific you are, the better. If your giftee is into Italian food, get them an Eataly gift card. If they're a PC gamer, get them a Steam card. If they're into education, a membership to Skillshare is perfect. There's a gift card out there for just about any interest, and all you have to do it google it and email it.

Generic gift cards can be a last-minute lifesaver that can still seem a little personal if you give them the right way.

Pick a theme or design: Many online cards, like Amazon, Etsy, or Starbucks, let you choose designs. The right visual makes the card feel more intentional.

Sources indicate that include a warm, personal message: Even one line can make a digital card feel thoughtful—something like, “I couldn’t pick just one thing for you. Hope this helps you treat yourself.”.

Send strategically: Deliver the card by email or text, but consider printing the email or screenshotting it in a small envelope so it feels like a “real” gift.

According to recent reports, sign someone up for a subscription service, write a note explaining you want to keep giving them presents all year, and you're golden. Here are some suggestions:.

SnackCrate: This service sends a different snack from around the world every month.

Industry observers note that spiceClub: For the culinary adventurer on your list. A subscription to RawSpiceBar’s Spice Club delivers a curated selection of spices every month.

Industry observers note that mocktail Club: Booze-free fancy drinks delivered once a month? Sign me up.

Thera Box: If you know someone in need of some self-care, this once-a-month box is packed with wellness and relaxation items.

Loot Crate: If your giftee is geeky, consider this monthly surprise box of pop culture treasures.

Cameo is a platform where celebrities, influencers, musicians, and performers create personalized video messages for fans. If someone on your list is a fan of someone on Cameo, you can set up a session, and give a card with a mysterious note like "Keep an eye out for a special message." They'll be delighted with a personal message from wrestling legend Mick Foley or terrified when Chris Hansen appears on their screen; your choice.

According to recent reports, I have enough crap in my house, so I love getting experiences instead of things. The challenge with experience gifts is usually timing: Many require reservations or coordination, but there are plenty of options that let your giftee schedule the time, making them perfect last-minute gifts.

Museum membership cards: Many institutions sell digital gift memberships that the recipient can activate whenever they like.

Movie tickets: Your local multiplex probably has a gift certificate you can buy online.

Local attraction passes: Some city attractions offer gift cards or “anytime admission” tickets that don’t expire immediately.

Pair these with a note explaining why you chose the experience, or, if you have that kind of relationship, something like, "I want to take you to the Museum of Modern Art." Just make sure you follow through and actually go.

It has been revealed that sometimes, there’s literally no time to order, wrap, or even think about a gift. If you’re scrambling out the door and need something now, you might be able to fake your way through, even if you're stopping at the liquor store on the way to the Christmas party.

Flowers or a small potted plant: Give a seasonal bouquet or a small indoor plant. Add a handwritten note, even a single line, and it might come off as thoughtful.

Gourmet chocolates or candy: Specialty chocolates from a local shop or grocery store display can feel luxe with a little ribbon or bag.

Recent findings suggest that wine, craft beer, or non-alcoholic beverage: A bottle with a clean label or interesting packaging immediately elevates your gift. Ask the clerk at the liquor store to help you find something unique.

Lottery tickets: Who wouldn't appreciate a bunch of scratch-off lottery tickets?

According to recent reports, hard cash is the most impersonal gift of all, but the only one you know will be used. This gift really depends on the person getting it, so be aware of whether they're likely to think "Just what I wanted!" or "Wait, I'm not poor." If you give cash, make sure it's crisp bills in a nice card, with a personalized note.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • After two weeks of voting that bracketed the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, Rockstar Games employees have voted overwhelmingly against a recognition agreement with the IWGB Game Workers Union.
  • 25% of Rockstar employees voted in favor of the recognition agreement, the union noted, while 75% voted against it.
  • According to recent reports, rockstar workers actually founded a union earlier this year—the Rockstar Game Workers Union, a subsidiary of the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain—and it will continue to operate as it has.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After two weeks of voting that bracketed the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, Rockstar Games employees have voted overwhelmingly against a recognition agreement with the IWGB Game Workers Union.

25% of Rockstar employees voted in favor of the recognition agreement, the union noted, while 75% voted against it. 1,544 employees took part in the vote, representing a turnout of just over 93%.

According to recent reports, rockstar workers actually founded a union earlier this year—the Rockstar Game Workers Union, a subsidiary of the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain—and it will continue to operate as it has. The IWGB said the outcome will not prevent Rockstar workers from organizing or exercising union rights, but the company will not be required to regularly meet with union representatives for collective bargaining or other relevant matters.

Despite the vote, the union remarked it will continue with organizing efforts at Rockstar.

Industry observers note that "For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society—this isn’t a sign to retreat, it’s a sign to double down on what we stand for. Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favour of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues," the IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union said. "We’re ready to put in the effort to make that happen.

"Whilst we haven’t emerged with a recognition deal, this ballot has put our union on the radar of every worker, and opened the door for upcoming kinds of conversation to start happening. People entirely unfamiliar with unions were for the first time debating employment conditions, collective bargaining rights, and our contracts. We heard from many more colleagues about what mattered to them, and we hope people will continue to engage so that we can see where these new discussions can lead us.".

The power to shape our working lives has always been, and always will be, in our hands.

In a separate statement, Rockstar head of publishing Jennfer Kolbe mentioned the studio is "extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we've built together and the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6.".

From the creators of Edge: A free weekly videogame industry newsletter, featuring in-depth news, expert analysis and exclusive interviews.

"This result reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong," Kolbe said. "As we look ahead, we're excited to build on all we've accomplished together.".

Recent findings suggest that rockstar, which said it worked with the IWGB to ensure employees were able to make an informed decision in a fair and transparent vote, came under fire in October 2025 for firing more than 30 employees, all of whom were members of a private trade union Discord channel. The IWGB called it "the most ruthless act of union busting in the history of the UK games industry," while Rockstar indicates they were fired for leaking information about "upcoming and unannounced games." That matter is now before an employment tribunal; closing submissions were made last week.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the Witcher 3 Remastered continues to recieve tweaks ahead of the Songs of the Past expansion arriving next year to whisk Gerry from the River off on a fresh adventure. Following some bloomin' improvements in October, its latest patch does a bunch of skill and mutation balancing, alongside further technical tweaks and fixes for some funky bugs.

In a recent development, "Fixed an issue where Reforging the Mastercrafted or Grandmaster Feline armor gave Geralt an unusual hairstyle," reads the first of numerous notes in the visual section of patch 5.02's notes about weird stuff happening to Gerry's luscious mane. "Fixed an issue where Geralt could become bald after enabling HairWorks on PC or Xbox Play Anywhere and then continuing the game on Xbox via Cross Progression," reads another that sounds slightly more serious. "Fixed an issue where growing a beard with the Rabble-rouser hairstyle made Geralt's head invisible," reads a third, which takes the cake.

There've also been instances of Gerry or NPCs missing their faces or "other body parts". The NPCs, bless them, have also had to deal with contracting "overly bright red areas on their legs" when moving through crowds. Oh, and a building near Novigrad's docks has been cheeklily disappearing whenever Geralt gets close to it. One would assume it's just a bit shy, though that's a tough thing to be when your location means people embarking and disembarking from ships are constantly walking past. To be honest, it also sounds like it could have been adapted into an extra contract for Gerry if CD Projekt had fancied. The studio have also "fixed an concern where installing and uninstalling mods could cause merchants' inventories, Geralt's inventory and storage to be emptied".

According to recent reports, beyond the giggle-worthy bug fixes, the most consequential aspect of the patch to my eye will likely be the tweaks to the power of certain skills and mutations, which folks may well be testing out if they're trying to settle on a new build before Songs of the Past. Those tweaks are as follows:.

Generally speaking, sign-heavy Gerry builds look like they'll be most acutely affected and be less effective following this patch. I typically only rely on Quen for a bit of shielding, because I'm an unimaginative monster slayer, so I'm not sure I'll notice it too much, but if you really make the most of your magical abilities it might hit your Gerry pretty hard.

It's worth skimming through the full notes if you've time, which also contain a few PC-specific fixes and tweaks. Starting a Hearts of Stone or Blood and Wine-only playthrough on Steam Deck should no longer lead to long load times, for example, while there've been some improvements made to path tracing and ray reconstruction .

According to recent reports, blizzard has officially unveiled Diablo 4's next live-service season: Season of Tyrael's Gambit. This is the ARPG's 16th season, and it follows on from the popular and well-received Season of Hell's Legacy.

In an unexpected move, Blizzard unveiled it's keeping some of the nostalgia-laiden content from the previous season, Season of Hell's Legacy, as a permanent addition. This is unusual, as the ephemeral nature of live seasons means new content goes away at the end of each season.

Season of Hell's Legacy paid tribute to Diablo's legacy and its 30th anniversary by introducing a lot of content inspired by previous Diablo games, chiefly Diablo 2. The list includes the return of iconic character Deckard Cain, a recreation of Old Tristram, and a major fight against the three Prime Evils - Diablo, Baal, and Mephisto - in their classic forms.

Sources indicate that "We heard overwhelming requests for features from Season of Hell's Legacy to carry forward as permanent game features," Blizzard wrote in Season 16's announcement post. "While the entire season couldn't come along for the ride, we are implementing the following features with the launch of Season of Tyrael's Gambit that will carry forward in both Eternal and Seasonal realms.".

So here's what's sticking around:.

In a recent development, season of Tyrael's Gambit kicks off 1st December, so you still have time to access all of that in Diablo 4 until Season 15 ends. Certain things, such as craftable items, won't return, so you may as well try them while you can. That mentioned, Blizzard is aware of the love some of those items have, and the developer said it may bring them back in the future.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that since the beginning of the week, the James Bond frenzy has shown no signs of stopping. On November 16, fresh Bond owners Amazon MGM Studios finally revealed the name of the actor who will succeed Daniel Craig as 007: Robert Pattinson. After years of speculation and months of intense rumors, the next James Bond now has a new face. Now, the next question on everyone’s mind: Who will be the next Bond girl?

Sources indicate that the exception in thie great debate is Léa Seydoux. The actor, who seems to be everywhere this year, played Madeleine Swann in Craig's final Bond films, Spectre (2015) and No Time to Die (2021). Her magnetic performance made Madeleine an unforgettable Bond girl, especially since her character plays a decisive role in the arc of Craig’s character: at the end of No Time to Die, the famous spy sacrifices himself to save her and their daughter, Mathilde. For the first time since its creation in 1953 by British author Ian Fleming, the secret agent in Her Majesty’s service was gone.

Léa Seydoux and Daniel Craig pose as they arrive on the set of No Time To Die on September 09, 2019 in Matera, Italy.

Recent findings suggest that in a recent interview on Vogue's The Run-Through podcast, Seydoux was candid about how little interest she had in her successor. “I don’t really care,” she said with a laugh. “I don’t really care, guys. How can you?”.

When pressed on who Pattinson's female lead might be, Seydoux expressed mixed feelings about the British spy's latest iteration. With the purchase of the Bond IP by Amazon, “It became American," Seydoux remarked. “But I’m sure the movie will be great because it’s directed by Denis Villeneuve, who’s a very talented director. I’m sure he will do something great.”.

Industry observers note that the online megamart took control of the storied franchise in 2023, after which Amazon founder Jeff Bezos controversially sought feedback on the title character's casting via X. The announcement of Villeneuve as the next film's director brought things back from the brink.

Recent findings suggest that bezos, who confirmed that he was “very involved” in the film's casting process, also seems to give Seydoux pause. In an interview with Variety, she admitted “was a bit sad when I heard that it was sold (…) but now that it’s Denis, I was like, Oh, at least it’s him, so it will be cinema.”.

Recent findings suggest that denis Villeneuve, who directed Seydoux in Dune: Part Two, will release the final installment of this epic science-fiction trilogy will be on December 16. After that, he'll be free to focus on his next major project: reviving the world’s most famous secret agent. It remains to be seen who he will choose to star opposite Robert Pattinson as his female companion—but we know that despite her fondness for the director, Seydoux will not return: Just last month, the French actress told People “I really loved being on this franchise, but now it’s ... done.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of Star Trek's most iconic fight scenes was also one of the most miserable to film. William Shatner recently talked about how bad it was to do the Gorn fight in the original series, and how it felt even worse to actually shoot than it looked onscreen.

It has been revealed that "Arena" is likely one of the most memorable episodes of Star Trek decades later. Unfortunately, that's not necessarily a great thing, as it contains (in my opinion) an obscenely bad fight scene. It's one in which Shatner's Kirk fights in slow motion with a member of the Gorn species. In addition to the iconic scene aging poorly, with effects that even looked dated back then, Shatner mentioned at Fresh York Comic Con it was also terrible to film (via Reddit):.

Recent findings suggest that the guy was in this rubber suit; it's 120 degrees in the desert. I have to roll in the regolith and get all dusty. And when you go to brush it off, you get blood.

Recent findings suggest that the "regolith," which by the way are the minerals that settle on top of bedrock, were so abrasive that it made the fight very difficult to film. I'm sure most Star Trek fans don't need to rewatch the scene with a Paramount+ subscription to know the end result ultimately wasn't worth the pain and toil. Still, lame fight aside, "Arena" is a pretty compelling episode.

I Just Found Out Wil Wheaton Apologized To Patrick Stewart After TNG, But I'm Not Surprised By The Captain's Response.

"Arena" starts when Kirk and the Gorn are transported to the planet to battle thanks to a third species named the Metrons. The Metrons wish to see a fight to the death, but are impressed when Kirk outmaneuvers the Gorn and spares its life instead. Both are then returned to their ship, with the lesson being that brains can overcome brawn with some quick thinking and skills.

It's great to hear William Shatner talk about the sillier times, as Star Trek fans were hit with some heavy news as of late. The passing of Walter Koenig was a gut punch to many, and following it with Patrick Stewart's death had many Trekkies out of the count. Shatner has even joked he's keeping an eye out for the Grim Reaper, trying to take the edge off such a heavy time.

Recent findings suggest that as for Star Trek in general, there's an overarching question about what direction the franchise is headed after its 60th anniversary. There's a movie in development, but with no solid timeline and no word that there are any shows actively being made, there are a lot of questions that still need to be answered.

In a recent development, for the time being, there's a lot of Star Trek to watch and enjoy over on Paramount+. Those who have never seen "Arena can go and check it out now for the first time, or some of the other classic Trek highlights as we wait for new entries in the franchise.

According to recent reports, things continue to get messy in the community of players working on getting Grand Theft Auto 6 working on PC. The previous frontrunner, Project Leonida, got their Discord server and GitHub repository taken down by Rockstar, but others have seemingly stepped in to finish the job.

Recent findings suggest that the most up-to-date build of GTA 6 was allegedly leaked earlier this week by notorious leaker CyberLeek. This is a supposedly near-final build of the game's Xbox version, and it's seemingly being used as the basis for the recent work to port the game to PC.

Unsurprisingly, most of these communities of modders rely almost exclusively on generative-AI tools like Claude and Antigravity to decompile and recompile the console version of GTA 6. That has always been the case, but the CyberLeek build only invited even more to ask AI chatbots to make the PC port for them.

X user chasm has been following developments in the GTA 6 decompile and recompile communities, and recently shared some of the prompts the so-called vibe-coders are using - a few of whom livestreamed the process.

According to recent reports, "Make no mistakes," one modder prompted the AI chatbot. "Keep finding more stuff and working and pushing," another eloquently asked. "Work faster," asked another. "There has to be a faster way to iterate than this," they continued.

In a recent development, as for how far some of the remaining communities have managed to get, this video allegedly shows the game running on PC. This goes beyond the boot-up screen, which modders were able to reach within hours of CyberLeek's build alleged leaking.

According to recent reports, the footage runs at sub-5fps, but the visuals look to have rendered normally. Assuming Rockstar doesn't also shut down the modders who remain active, we may see another progress update.

In as booming a monster truck rally commentator voice as you can imagine: ARE YOU READY TO GET DECIMATED??? Yes? Yippee! Because I've got some good news for you. The latest revision for Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2 is here, appropriately dubbed the Decimation update, which adds in a fresh mode and more.

In a recent development, first up, that new mode! It's called Weekly Clash and it's for the competitive folks out there. "This new PvP shakes things up with the introduction of “Weekly Clash”, a new mode that brings unique new rules to Eternal War, like games restricted to a single class, a single weapon or even granting near-unlimited grenades," explains a Steam blog post. "Except more modifiers to be added in the future.".

It has been revealed that this enhancement also introduces a fresh Chaos Siege sector, that new mode introduced last month, which adds in a "new playable sector bringing a renewed challenge between waves 11 and 15!" You'll also find six new heroic weapons in the armoury, like the omnissian axe, plasma incinerator and heavy bolter. This comes complete with some new heroic armour pieces, specifically four new helmets. On top of all of this, there's been a Vanguard rework: "Fight the enemies of Humanity with new ways to use your Grapnel Launcher! Attack cancellations, close-quarter kicks and a new Revenge mechanic make the Vanguard as bold and brutal as he’s ever been!".

Some other general tweaks have been made with this patch too. All PvP maps have seen the number and locations of ammo and equipment pickups adjusted, and conditions for the spawn position swap system have been improved. A level lock for the Absolute Siege and Absolute Stratagems mode has also been added; "The difficulty will be accessible to Classes that have reached level 25 or achieved Prestige at least once." And you'll also find that loading times and general connectivity should be a bit better!

Latest Update: Where to find GTA 6's UFO and alien

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1273 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 might feel more grounded compared to its predecessors, but that doesn't mean Leonida isn't full of weird and supernatural ongoings.
  • Industry observers note that and if you don't know where to look, here's where I can help you.
  • The alien abduction is actually a three-parter mission, and to get started you'll first need to locate the abandoned car.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 might feel more grounded compared to its predecessors, but that doesn't mean Leonida isn't full of weird and supernatural ongoings. One such paranormal activity is GTA 6's aliens—if you know where to look, you'll be able to find a UFO which'll eventually lead you down a strange road of cows, radiation, and the aliens themselves.

Industry observers note that and if you don't know where to look, here's where I can help you. If you want to find GTA 6's UFO and a weird little alien guy, here's exactly where you need to go and what you need to do.

The alien abduction is actually a three-parter mission, and to get started you'll first need to locate the abandoned car. You'll need to look for it at nighttime, and it can spawn in a number of locations. For me, it was a little ways east of Port Gellhorn in Kelly County. For our own Chris Livingston, he discovered the car somewhere north of Capri, also in Kelly County. You know it's the one if the car is pointed toward a forest and the doors are open.

Once you've found it, you'll need to follow the path it's parked along. You'll know you're going the right way by the clothes strewn along the path. If it's a bit too dark or you're stuck, you can press L3 + R3 to activate your focus and see the clothes more easily or equip your flashlight. Eventually you'll see the lights of the UFO and a very naked lady amongst it all. Head over until a cutscene plays out.

Once that's over, you'll get into a light scuffle with the woman before she instructs you to go get her car. Head back to where you first found the vehicle, where one more cutscene will play out and you'll be done… for now.

It has been revealed that you'll need to wait for some time to pass. Make sure you're heading home and going to sleep each night, preferably as whichever character you discovered the UFO on. Eventually, you'll trigger a cutscene that'll bring you to a white room.

Recent findings suggest that find the dark oval which signals the way to a corridor and run through it. You'll be met with a terrifying maze of eggs. Get close to them and they'll start glowing blue. Get too close and they'll turn yellow, eventually cracking and causing your character to be yoinked back to the start by tentacles.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Industry observers note that carefully make your way through the eggs, finding large gaps where you won't cause them to break. Once you've made it to the other side, you'll be met with another room containing the solar system. Take a look at earth—this is actually showing you where you'll need to head for part three of this mission—and continue onwards until you reach a code.

Industry observers note that to decipher the code, simply look at how many lines are in each of the four symbols above the keypad. For me, the code was 3124. Punch in the code, and head to the next room.

Here, you'll need to push the button on the control panel and light it up. The aim is to have four green lights, so keep pushing until all four are the same colour and then pull the lever to the left.

Once that's done, you'll be met with three metal doors. The middle one'll do some nasty damage if you step into the room and hang around too long, so avoid it. Instead, head to the room on the left—yes, the one with the cows—and run in to grab the bottle of milk on the table.

Industry observers note that run back out and head for the door on the right. Walk to the end until you see a contraption where you're able to insert your milk bottle. Shortly after, you'll wake up back in your bed and ready to tackle the final part of this mission chain.

Industry observers note that you'll want to head over to the location shown to you in the globe. More specifically, you'll want to head south of Hamlet, at this abandoned building just west of the river.

There'll be a gap in the fence you can hop over, or you can shoot the padlock, or alternatively ram into the gate with your car. From here, you can either climb on top of the roof and drop down or find the double doors and kick them down, or use the snap gun. Either way, you'll want to make sure the door is unlocked for later in this mission.

Turn around and head down the stairs, towards the keypad at the end of the corridor. The code here is the same as the one you used earlier, so punch it in again and head into the elevator.

Walk through the tunnel and you'll once again be met with a control panel and three doors, plus a little audiotape with some fun exposition about alien experimentation. You'll be doing the exact same thing here as you did earlier—get every light to green, push the lever, and head into the left room to retrieve a bottle of milk. The middle room once again doles out gnarly damage, so don't hang too long or avoid it all together.

Head over to the door on the right, down the corridor and into the room. Insert the milk bottle into the contraption and after a few seconds, out will pop a little alien guy! It's unconscious, though, so you'll need to pick it up.

According to recent reports, as soon as you've picked up the alien, the bunker will begin to fill with toxic gas and you'll need to head out ASAP. Go back the way you came—through the tunnel and into the elevator, and then through those double doors you snap gunned/kicked down earlier to get outside.

Sadly, your time with this alien fella is brief, as it'll promptly get beamed up into the sky by a UFO. It also doesn't take long for special forces to show up, but don't worry. The UFO will return to laser them all down, allowing you to get out without any further concerns.

Recent findings suggest that for your troubles, the aliens will give you a permanent buff to your health, stamina, and focus, so helping out these extraterrestrials is more than worth the effort. And, y'know, the trauma.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 was subject to more than a few leaks in the run-up to its eventual launch, but despite it all, one major early-game twist was kept a total secret until release – something Rockstar Games boss Rob Nelson was "praying" for.

Before we get into it, we're obviously about to discuss some spoilers for GTA 6 Chapter 1. It's an early moment – one you'll have seen if you've played the first hour of the game – but if you're yet to dive in, you might want to bookmark this to come back to later. Or, of course, feel free to carry on if you don't care about a spoiler-free experience.

Everyone still here who wants to be? Great. As you probably guessed, the twist in question is the existence of Jason and Lucia's son, Tomás.

After being moved to her aunt's care following her arrest, as shown in the game's prologue, Lucia's primary motivation is to get Tomás back and give him a good life alongside Jason, but none of this was revealed prior to launch – officially or otherwise. This was something that co-studio head of Rockstar North, Rob Nelson, had his "fingers crossed" for.

Industry observers note that in an interview with VGC a few days before GTA 6's launch, Nelson confirmed that Rockstar was "never" planning to reveal the twist and, at the time, was still praying no one would spill the beans ahead of schedule. "I am still holding on," he said. "Fingers crossed, how many more days? I'm praying it stays under wraps. Given everything that we've gone through, every day I'm just like, 'please, please don't do that, please don't do that.'".

While VGC notes that there was a small amount of chatter on forums about Jason and Lucia having a son, these whispers generally didn't stick, and, notably, none of the Cyberleek videos that appeared online before launch revealed Tomás. Honestly, that feels somewhat miraculous given how early he's revealed and how frequently he comes up in the story and dialogue.

Cyberleek wasn't the only hacker to target Rockstar, either – there was also an enormous wave of GTA 6 leaks in 2022 – but even so, no baby boy and the driving force of the plot were plastered all over the internet as a result.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

Anyway, however the bullet was dodged, it made for an excellent twist, and let Rockstar have the story moment it was hoping for. "It's meant to shock," Nelson explained. "We were watching everyone speculate about the nature of their relationship and Jason's character, and that takes it in a completely different context. You have something to strive for beyond a huge bank account at the end.".

The Method-Dressing Madness Behind Mckenna Grace’s ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Press Tour Looks

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Before the Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping press tour began, Mckenna Grace knew she wanted to be method dressed for her appearances.

  • In a wide-ranging conversation, Dickson breaks down all the looks that set the Hunger Games fans’ hearts aflame, from Rue’s blue dress to Katniss’ Mockingjay gown, and all the threads that came together for Grace’s most memorable press appearances yet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Before the Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping press tour began, Mckenna Grace knew she wanted to be method dressed for her appearances. Made a household term by Law Roach and Zendaya, method dressing is when actors wear looks that pay homage to the film or show they’re promoting: See Zendaya’s on-theme looks across red carpets for Dune, Spiderman, and The Odyssey for a slew of examples.

Industry observers note that with the new Hunger Games film, it’s Grace’s turn to adopt the trend. A super fan of the Suzanne Collins book series and their film adaptations, Grace—who plays District 12 tribute Maysilee Donner—took a hand in the styling for her press run, weaving easter eggs into every look. Her stylist, Molly Dickson, was up for the challenge of translating Grace’s deep-cut references into custom and archival looks from Monique Lhuillier, Gucci, Celine and more.

In a wide-ranging conversation, Dickson breaks down all the looks that set the Hunger Games fans’ hearts aflame, from Rue’s blue dress to Katniss’ Mockingjay gown, and all the threads that came together for Grace’s most memorable press appearances yet.

Vanity Fair: How did you get into styling?

Molly Dickson: I went to college in Minnesota and my major was advertising. Two weeks before I graduated, I called my mom and said, "I'm not into this. I don't wanna do advertising." She said, "Well, what do you wanna do?" I told her, "I wanna do fashion. I wanna go to New York." She said, "No, absolutely not.".

Industry observers note that right after I graduated, I went to LA, this was 2009 during the recession, and no one was hiring. I got an internship at Marie Claire in Newly introduced York, and enrolled back into college to get school credit to intern at Hearst. I worked at Marie Claire as a market assistant for almost two years, and then I left and assisted Leslie Fremar for seven years. That's when I fell in love with celebrity. Then ten years ago, I went off on my own.

What would you say are your aesthetic influences as a stylist?

My personal style relates very similarly to Sadie Sink's style, very effortless. She always wants to be very comfortable and easy, never anything frilly or over the top. Just a simple, beautiful dress, and you let it speak for itself.

In a recent development, mckenna is a big fan of the original film series, so it’s clear you’re pulling from there as influences when dressing her. Is it a collaborative process when coming to one of these referential looks?

Recent findings suggest that she's obviously a very huge fan of the franchise. We actually started having conversations about this tour in April, which is very early to start having conversations. I could just sense her excitement around it. She started sending me mood boards, and I actually looked back today at the mood board and it was, it was a lot of Katniss Everdeen. It had Joanna on it, and it was filled with these really strong female characters from the franchise.

What she really wanted to hit was Katniss’ wedding gown look and the Mockingjay look with the wings. I was really stumped on how to pull that off without making it overly costumey.

Mckenna kept asking, "What's going on with those?" I knew the vision, but I didn't know how to execute it. I was working with Keke Palmer and the designer Michael Ngo. He was making some cool music costumes for Keke, and I asked, "Michael, could you make this silver piece?" 'Cause I really had no idea how to get it done.

Sources indicate that he noted, “I don't think I can do that. You know what? Just give me a day, let me play around with it." That night, he said, "I figured it out." We got the piece and I thought, "Okay, it needs to be a wedding dress under,” so I reached out to all the bridal houses. I wanted it to be vintage because it would tell a pretty story. Monique [Lhuillier] ended up sending a ton of wedding gowns, and the day before Mckenna came in for the fitting, I actually tried the wedding dresses on myself with the silver piece.

I sent Mckenna five dresses, and the one that she ended up wearing, she noted, "That's it. I don't even need to try anything else. That's the one I'm gonna wear." Then, it was a matter of finding the right event to wear it to because it’s pretty nice, very dramatic.

According to recent reports, she was in Paris for the Miu Miu show, and I brought it there because she had the Hunger Games Museum event. It was a whole conversation with her team, like, "Is it the right moment? Is it too much for this event?" Her PR remarked, "No, this is the perfect moment. It's the best way to kick off the tour." The response with the Hunger Games fans—I have never seen anything like it before, ever.

What was the experience of having her be such a substantial part of the styling process?

It makes my job so fun because she is so passionate about it and she loves Hunger Games so much, even just finding subtle nods back to the movie. She would say, "I wanna do a ladybug look." Thom Browne did that amazing ladybug dress, I thought, "That's so cool, but it's not really her personal aesthetic." So it’s finding ways to keep it still true to her personal style while maintaining the nods to the film.

The way you seem to understand Mckenna feels something similar to the connection between Katniss and Cinna in The Hunger Games. When pulling looks for her, what comes into play? How do you make her come through and not be lost in the lore of the stories or the dress?

Mckenna had noted that she maybe wanted to do a red or a dark pink feather look because in the books [Maysilee] gets attacked by the red birds which are like flamingos. I'm pulling in all these red feather dresses and on the runway, this one dress looked amazing. Mckenna said, “That's perfect for the flamingo reference.”.

According to recent reports, but we put it on her and it was so big, and she's so petite so she was just getting swarmed. I said, “Let"s not force it.” The goal was for her to feel comfortable in the look rather than just getting each reference.

Recent findings suggest that the public has been really excited about these looks. Are you thinking about the response to the looks when you’re putting them together?

There's been some conversations in a fitting, like, "Oh, the Hunger Games fans are gonna get this." They're gonna see the inspiration, they're gonna understand it.

But I wouldn't say we're choosing a look because ‘Oh, this is gonna go viral to the Hunger Games community.’ Mckenna is a super fan herself so if she's getting excited about the look, everyone else that's a fan of the franchise is gonna get excited about the look.

Mckenna Grace in Betsey Johnson.

Do you feel any pressure to top the last outfit after each premiere?

Yes. I think it was Paris because that wedding dress did get so much press. In that fitting, it felt like, "We gotta keep our game up high." It's been really fun for my team and market assistants because a lot of the girls that work with me are huge fans of the movie. They're not even seeing it as work. They're like, "Oh my God, this is so exciting. Look at this. This looks like this from the movie.".

Sources indicate that what was the inspiration to do method dressing for this press run? What do you think is the value?

Sources indicate that mckenna knew back in April, she said, "I wanna do method for this." I personally did not read the books. I'm a visual person, so I've seen all the movies. Lionsgate was able to let me go with the cast when they first saw the movie because my agent was like, "Molly needs to go to the movie to get inspired before this press tour. She can't do a method dressing press tour without seeing the movie.".

Even as the tour was going on, Mckenna kept sending me upcoming references and quotes from the book and stuff like that.

It has been revealed that what made you take it to the next level? From paying homage to not only characters, but the actual actors from the films like Jennifer Lawrence at the 2011 Oscars to even dressing like set pieces from the film.

According to recent reports, that was all Mckenna's vision. On her first mood board, she had a lot of Jennifer Lawrence's red carpet moments because she's such a huge fan of Katniss and Jennifer Lawrence.

According to recent reports, with the Rue reference, Mckenna thought that color was just very Hunger Games. It wasn't until she put the dress on, her mom mentioned, "Wait, this is Rue's dress." So that was just fate. I would love to take credit for that.

Why do you think that this styling has generated so much attention?

According to recent reports, I think it’s when you do method dressing for such a big franchise and you really are passionate about it. The thing is that Mckenna is so excited and passionate about this movie. She has said, “I didn't think that I would love doing fittings so much. I used to hate doing fittings.”.

Mckenna Grace in Elisabetta Franchi.

Because every look is so intentionally tied back to Hunger Games and she's such a massive fan, it's literally like playing dress up with her. I think the fans see it, she's so relatable because she's a fan that all these fans think, "Wow, like, she's a fan and she got to do this." She’s the fangirl living out her dream, and the fans are excited for her that she finally gets to do this.

What do you think are the best kinds of projects to implement method dressing with/works best with? What does it work best with?

Sources indicate that I think the big movies that already have a fan base, like Barbie or Wednesday, Being able to pull inspiration from existing books or films makes it so much easier for a stylist rather than a movie that no one's seen before. There's no curiosity or momentum about it because you're starting from scratch, whereas Hunger Games, Barbie, Wednesday, there's already a level of expectation.

The looks for this press run have been a mix of archival, new, and custom pieces. How do you make that choice? How important is it for you to create an archive for Mckenna?

It kind of is a mix of what we’re able to source. Mckenna really wanted to pay homage to Joanna's character with that scene where she's like, "My stylist is always putting me in trees." She's like, "I wanna do a tree reference." And I'm like, "How in the world am I gonna find a fashion reference that's a tree that's not a costume?".

Recent findings suggest that I love the challenge of sourcing the market, and so do the girls on my team. I think it was 2011 Phoebe Philo where Celine did some tree references in the collection. But just because we find it online doesn't mean that we can get it. So then it's reaching out to every vintage dealer, every rental house, asking, "Do you guys have anything like this?" And they might have it, but they're like, "It's already gone, someone has it." I ended up actually finding the Celine tree dress on the RealReal, and I bought it. I love RealReal.

What is your approach to dressing different clients? For instance, you mentioned Sadie Sink earlier, can you walk me through how that process differs from Mckenna?

It's very different between each girl. I let them set the pace. If they wanna be involved, great. If they just wanna show up to the fitting and not even know what's gonna be there, I try to accommodate whatever direction they wanna go. I have one client that literally last week has sent me over 200 references of dresses that she wants, and another girl that's like, “I really don't care. Whatever you tell me to wear, I'll wear it.”.

According to recent reports, every girl is different, and what makes my job so interesting is that it's not the same. Everyone has very different styles. I think the most crucial part of a job as a stylist is to keep their style true to them and not just force my style onto them. Mckenna's way more girly, Sadie is a little bit more casual, it’s just taking their style and elevating it a little bit.

According to recent reports, will you do any looks inspired by Mckenna’s character Maysilee? The looks have been mostly referential to things and people from past stories. Are there influences of Maysilee in the looks that fans haven't been able to pick up on because the film wasn’t out yet?

In a recent development, in a couple days, she’ll be in Miami for press, and she's wearing a very Maysilee inspired, purple Miu Miu dress that has a white collar. When she wears it, everyone's gonna be like, "Oh, that's Maysilee." She really wanted to have flowers and necklaces because Maysilee is really into jewelry, so it’s very light and flowery.

Can you break down the outfit for the Upcoming York City premiere?

We are doing the Mockingjay dress, the one with the wings, and that was another thing that I was very stumped on. I'm like, "What designer's gonna make these wings?" I had this woman in LA who does wings, she's done Halloween costumes and music videos.

Mckenna Grace in Pamella Roland.

In a recent development, in the first fitting, I pulled this navy Pamella Roland gown. The fabric is really, really cool. It's like a shimmery kind of organza. I thought, "That's the right color,” but I wanted it to be strapless. I went back to Pamella Roland and they were like, "We can make it in strapless." Mckenna was very keen on having some sort of embellishment to replicate Katniss because she had screen printing on the gown and it kind of looks like wings in a way.

It has been revealed that pamella then drew all these CADs with diamond wings on it, and then we got the wings made. We did the final fitting and I almost started to cry. Her mom's taking videos and it's epic. It's so exciting because the fans were doing polls on what she's gonna wear to the premiere.

It's full circle, we started with the wedding dress, Mckenna did the fire gown, and then we ended with the Mockingjay dress.

What was the hardest look to pull together?

Mckenna Grace in custom Cong Tri.

I think design-wise, it was the fire gown.

It has been revealed that getting the fire printed on the fabric was really hard. I had a while back done a custom Cong Tri gown for Cami Mendes for the Masters of the Universe tour. It was like a gold beaded gown, and I remember I really liked the fabrics that they used for it.

Industry observers note that so when I was thinking of who could do this fire gown, I reached out to them first, and I'm like, "Can you guys do something that looks like a fire? Like, she's literally on fire." And they're like, "No. We don't think we can." And again, they were like, "Give us some time." They came back and stated, "We did all these testing on the fabric." I'm like, "Yeah, you did it. You did it.".

According to recent reports, what's really funny is we were at a fitting at Mckenna's house with the fire gown in a garment bag, and one of her friends stopped by. It was just a tip of the dress showing and her friend said, "Oh my God, you got a fire gown." Then I thought, "Okay, people are gonna get it.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • As World of Warcraft: Forever players dived into the game, they quickly discovered a specific weapon enchant that took area of effect spells to a whole other level.
  • The enchantment in question was Revelation - a fresh addition to the game included as part of the new trade good reputations.
  • So for example, let's say you're a druid casting the Hurricane spell.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As World of Warcraft: Forever players dived into the game, they quickly discovered a specific weapon enchant that took area of effect spells to a whole other level. Sadly, with a sudden hotfix last night, this particular use case for the enchant has been removed.

The enchantment in question was Revelation - a fresh addition to the game included as part of the new trade good reputations. What it does is simple: when you fail to deal a critical strike with a spell, the next spell hit is guaranteed to do so. What made this particularly powerful is that the buff also worked with continuous area of effect spells, meaning an early instance of the spell not crit-ing would result in the remaining damage hits all dealing critical damage.

So for example, let's say you're a druid casting the Hurricane spell. This is a channel spell with a total of 10 seconds of cast time. Every second, it deals damage. If the first instance of damage at the one second mark doesn't crit, the remaining nine instances of damage would all crit. This resulted in absurd amounts of damage, and made players of druids, warlocks, and mages very happy.

While strong enchantments are often pricey, this was notably cheap, due to the low-cost of resources used to create it and the low requirements to learn it. As such, people were spending a handful of gold for an early game enchantment that was being actively used all the way into the end game.

It was admittedly a tad too strong, and the effect triggered on AOE spells was almost certainly an unintended effect of the enchantment. Last night, the fun came to an end. Now, the effect is used up as intended in long-casted spells. So going back to the example given, if the first instance of damage on Hurricane doesn't crit, then the second one still will. However, this will use up the effect, and the third instance of damage will revert to regular ol' damage numbers. It also seems as though it Revelation can't trigger more than once during a single channeled spell.

This is the latest in a string of ongoing quickfire bug fixes and game adjustments being made to World of Warcraft: Forever. The devs have been continuously updating the game in an attempt to curb certain gold farms, following the discovery of a particularly lucrative Blackmaw Hold gold exploit. The dev team has expressed some interesting ideas for the game longterm, including a desire to kill best-in-slot gear.

  • According to recent reports, HARK THE GHOUL releases 👉JANUARY 21st, 2027!!!👈 Our action-adventure RPG built around freeform exploration lets you loose in a dark Victorian city full of secrets to uncover and ravenous monsters to defeat!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I'm a simple person. I see an anthropomorphic rat man who opens up his trench coat that is filled with regular rats in the same manner as one would with counterfeit watches in a trailer for a video game, I add it to my wishlist. There really isn't much I need in life, but that certainly fulfills those needs. And it's exactly what HARK THE GHOUL is offering, an action-adventure, dungeon crawler RPG set in a weird and nasty Victorian gothic city with an emphasis on free exploration.

Now, I appreciate not all of you will be as immediately convinced by trench coat wearing rat men, so let's have a deeper gander at the game together. Exploration really does seem to be the key thing here, not just in terms of going wherever you want, more or less when you want, but how you get about. For example, say there's an annoying gap you want to cross. Use a magical spell to summon a crate, then lob it in front of you, and cast some icey magic to freeze it into place, thereby creating a fresh platform for you to hop onto. Looks like nice and systemic stuff!

According to recent reports, HARK THE GHOUL releases 👉JANUARY 21st, 2027!!!👈 Our action-adventure RPG built around freeform exploration lets you loose in a dark Victorian city full of secrets to uncover and ravenous monsters to defeat! Coming to Steam, Switch 1, Switch 2, PS5 and Xbox Series![image or embed].

Recent findings suggest that this extends to the combat, which faces you against odd automatons, infected foes and nasty beasties. You can perform quite silly tricks like using your shovel to dig up a rock and chuck that at a baddie, or you can use your magic to conjure up an explosive crate which you then kick at an enemy, blasting it with a shotgun. It appears to almost be an RPG by way of the immersive sim; there's no correct way to go about the game, only the way you find most fun. Though maybe that's dredging up the debate around what an immersive sim is….

Either way, I'm just tickled pink by HARK THE GHOUL, which also pits you as a mothman-type figure who's just emerged from their cocoon. Delightful! And it just got a release date too: January 21st, 2027. That's only a couple of months away, obviously, but if you can't wait that long then there's a demo you can check out on Steam. Or, you know, just throw it a wishlist! Offering it some support either way seems like a nice idea.

#143262. Aspects of GTA 6 are inspired by Red Dead Redemption 2's honor system because its player agency 'was a hard thing to ignore and walk away from'

Aspects of GTA 6 are inspired by Red Dead Redemption 2's honor system because its player agency 'was a hard thing to ignore and walk away from'

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (684 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 doesn't just mark a huge, and at times unbelievable, step forward for graphics; it's also at the forefront of what an open world game can be, just look at the existential crisis it's given Cyberpunk 2's creative director.
  • Industry observers note that "As the resolution goes up, you want the sophistication of the experience to go up, and obviously the sophistication of the mechanics," Rob Nelson, Rockstar's head of development, claims in an interview with Eurogamer.
  • Sources indicate that the sophisticated mechanics that Nelson is talking about here pertains to GTA 6's Criminal Profile, a system that evaluates your escapades across Leonida and gives you a rating.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 doesn't just mark a huge, and at times unbelievable, step forward for graphics; it's also at the forefront of what an open world game can be, just look at the existential crisis it's given Cyberpunk 2's creative director. With thousands of enterable buildings, unpredictable and slightly scary NPCs, and systems that help you determine what kind of criminal you want to be. It all really does feel like a milestone for what videogames can do.

Industry observers note that "As the resolution goes up, you want the sophistication of the experience to go up, and obviously the sophistication of the mechanics," Rob Nelson, Rockstar's head of development, claims in an interview with Eurogamer. "So it just naturally flowed that we give players choices to interact with the world beyond just violence, beyond just 'down the barrel of a gun', because it's fun.".

Sources indicate that the sophisticated mechanics that Nelson is talking about here pertains to GTA 6's Criminal Profile, a system that evaluates your escapades across Leonida and gives you a rating. There's Professional, Hardened, Violent, Psycho, and Irredeemable. The more stealthy and non-lethal you are, the higher your profile will be. It's similar to Red Dead Redemption 2's Honor System.

In a recent development, "There was maybe more emotional resonance in the story of RDR2 than we had, certainly in a GTA before," Nelson says. "So we liked that idea. We didn't necessarily come to GTA 6 going: 'We must have emotional resonance,' but all of those things combine. It's more that those systems and that element of player choice and agency, and the way that affected the narrative, was a hard thing to ignore and walk away from.".

Nelson explains that most of the groundwork started as "simple things" in principle, "but they create a lot more work in terms of development of the sophistication of the systems." It's all about choice in GTA 6. You choose whether you want to be a criminal with a conscience or a loose cannon.

"It's still a world of violence, but you could threaten somebody by aiming a gun at them and just robbing them, and they have a chance to comply. So you don't have to beat them to death to get their money.".

The part that sticks out the most is that you "don't have to" approach crimes in a certain way, there's still the option to go into every encounter guns blazing because redemption only works from a storytelling perspective when it's the player's choice, and not as Nelson puts it, something that is "foisted upon you".

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

"You can still go on those rampages and basically smash your Criminal Profile until it breaks," Nelson adds. "And then you enter this irredeemable state, which basically claims, 'I reject your criminal profile system! I don't want it.'".

Am I brave enough to reject the criminal profile system entirely? Hell no. I replay sections of dialogue if I accidentally upset someone, and cannot do an "evil run" of a game without giving myself stomach ulcers because of the guilt—but I appreciate having the option.

#143260. Why did Rockstar Games make empathy a key mechanic in GTA 6? "Because it's fun" indicates head of development Rob Nelson

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1494 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Eurogamer ↗ Open Full Page

Why did Rockstar Games make empathy a key mechanic in GTA 6? "Because it's fun" indicates head of development Rob Nelson

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1494 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There's been plenty of chatter about Grand Theft Auto 6's 'honour system', so to speak, implemented here via what the game calls your Criminal Profile.
  • In a recent development, our own Dom just wrote that they prefer to turn its notifications off, for instance, in favour of fully soaking into the immersion.
  • According to recent reports, some of that is genuinely interesting - I'm dubious as to whether that's really what this system is doing, for a start.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There's been plenty of chatter about Grand Theft Auto 6's 'honour system', so to speak, implemented here via what the game calls your Criminal Profile.

In a recent development, our own Dom just wrote that they prefer to turn its notifications off, for instance, in favour of fully soaking into the immersion. Personally I quite like the pop-ups - I find the act of figuring out systems and how they're manipulated almost as fun as the games they're a part of. And pop-ups or no, the fact that GTA 6 can arguably be portrayed as 'rewarding' empathy and 'discouraging' the series' famous rampages of mass violence has sparked a fair bit of debate.

According to recent reports, some of that is genuinely interesting - I'm dubious as to whether that's really what this system is doing, for a start. Is it incentivising and disincentivising certain in-game behaviour, or just putting a label on it? And then, actually: does the act of labelling "psycho" behaviour alone actually become a disincentivising factor in itself?

Either way, until now Rockstar hasn't said a great deal about why, exactly, this system - seen by some as one that builds empathy into GTA's chaotic world - was implemented in the first place. But during an interview I had with Rob Nelson, Rockstar Games' head of development, just before GTA 6's launch earlier this month, a little more on that came to light.

Recent findings suggest that A little context is necessary here: Nelson's response was actually following a question I had about the overall approach to design that Rockstar took, and how its wider themes and intentions came about. As a part of that, he turned to this system - and how, in a way, it exists here because of the work the studio simply didn't want to leave behind after Red Dead Redemption 2.

Sources indicate that nelson explained that this all began when the team was in the early phase of exploring what type of game GTA 6 would be, in 2015 and 2016, while much of the studio was still working full-tilt on RDR2 - a game which itself didn't release until late 2018. The team was looking to "build up the sophistication of the NPC population, and also allow for more player choice than we had [before], and more options in terms of the way you interact with the world beyond just violence," Nelson told me.

The idea would be that "it's still a world of violence - but you could threaten somebody by aiming a gun at them and just robbing them, and they have a chance to comply. So you don't have to beat them to death to get their money." Ideas that were "simple things" in principle, he remarked, "but they create a lot more work in terms of development of the sophistication of the systems.".

Then, as systems were gradually implemented, it became a question of "trying to marry up what you're doing in the open world with who we're saying you are in the narrative - more than we had, I would say, previously, in Red Dead 2." It's here where the system now referred to as the Criminal Profile started to form.

The thinking turned to "the nature of 'honour', which wasn't always a part of it" with Red Dead Redemption 2, Nelson continued, "but became part of it as we were working on this story and finding that the 'redemption arc' didn't feel so good when it was foisted upon you - and feelings that we had playing Red Dead sort of early on." (Those feelings, primarily, were around getting you to invest in a gang led by Dutch Van der Linde, who was fundamentally unlikable from the off - or plain "crazy", as Nelson put it. The implementation of more player choices and agency was part of Rockstar's way to build investment in Arthur, even as he followed Dutch.).

That meant moving the choices away from key story moments, where many games tend to put them. Instead, Rockstar built a system that ran alongside the story via smaller, moment-to-moment choices you might make. "We tried to take all of those off the main flow and make them optional. So again, they're a choice.".

"Usually they involve some form of slight sacrifice or more effort on the part of the player," he added. The hope, then, was that you as a player would both "feel something", and ultimately also feel "you got the outcome that you deserved.".

According to recent reports, that was the initial thinking behind this kind of system as a whole. Coming to GTA 6, it then combined with a wider desire to "evolve" Grand Theft Auto as both the team's storytelling and the available technology matured. "You're thinking about story and character set, but we're also thinking about what we want to do with GTA as a series, and how you want to evolve it," Nelson mentioned.

"I think as the resolution goes up, it sort of asks different latest questions," he continued. "As the resolution goes up, you want the sophistication of the experience to go up, and obviously the sophistication of the mechanics. So it just naturally flowed that we give players choices to interact with the world beyond just violence, beyond just 'down the barrel of a gun', because it's fun.".

"It's fun for some people like myself to just sort of role-play in the world, and be in the world, and restraint becomes something you hadn't thought about," he continued. That tied back into the more sophisticated NPCs and reactions the team were making.

"If you think about the NPCs, even back to [GTA] 5, you would draw a weapon - first of all, they didn't react if you drew an invisible shotgun out of nowhere, or a rocket launcher," he noted. "They don't react unless you aim it, and then they flee in terror, and you're just sort of this demigod stomping through the world, you know? And that's fun, but for how long?

It has been revealed that "The team then started thinking of ways to build a bit more sustained enjoyment from it. "What if you can't do that?" Nelson continued. What if, instead of whipping an RPG out of nowhere, "you have to call your car. You have to pop a car trunk and get it, and now I'm walking, and now people are noticing, but they're sort of sidling away, and it's more believable. And then they're still fleeing in terror, but then there's people who also have guns, and they're shooting at you, or you try to hold somebody up and they pull a gun, or they grab it, and then you have to deal with them.

"And then, he continued, "you choose. You're trying to jack somebody off a motorcycle, and they pull a gun on you, and you have to blow their head off and it's like, 'You shouldn't have made me do that!' And so then it has more meaning, and it's more funny in a way when it's a little bit more pointed. And you can still go on those rampages and basically smash your Criminal Profile until it breaks and then you enter this irredeemable state, which basically notes 'I reject your criminal profile system! I don't want it.'".

Sources indicate that that Irredeemable profile level, for what it's worth, was another element born of Red Dead Redemption 2. "We had that with Red Dead, where people would sort of have low honour, and then 'greet' their way back up to high honour. And so this was an attempt of sorts of [making something] for people that just want to go crazy and almost opt out of the system. They can opt out of it - and you can also turn off the notifications in the system.".

It's notable, in fact, just how interlinked the thinking was with GTA 6 and Red Dead Redemption 2. As Nelson put it at one point: "There was maybe more emotional resonance in the story of RDR2 than we had had, certainly in a GTA before. So we liked that idea." What Rockstar did with GTA 6 was then in a way a natural next step. "We didn't necessarily come to GTA 6 going: 'We must have emotional resonance,' but all of those things combine. It's more that those systems and that element of player choice and agency, and the way that affected the narrative, was a hard thing to ignore and walk away from.".

We'll have much more like this from our interview with Nelson very soon, so do look out for that on Eurogamer over the coming days. In the meantime, we've a handy guide explaining exactly how GTA 6's Criminal Profile system works and how to change, raise, or lower that profile if you're in need of a deep dive into how it all really works.
