💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the industry's in a troubling position right now.
  • Recent findings suggest that chris Wilson, former lead designer on Path of Exile and co-founder of Grinding Gear Games, discussed the merits of Larian's approach with Destin on YouTube.
  • According to recent reports, "They made it, they had a good extended early access period for getting feedback without spoiling the game, and they released it in a sincere way," he explains.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the industry's in a troubling position right now. Layoffs are widespread, triple-A budgets have ballooned, and it seems harder than ever to know what'll make a game stick. In the mind of one of the central devs on the Path of Exile series, Baldur's Gate 3 is a strong example of the kind of business model studios should aspire toward.

Recent findings suggest that chris Wilson, former lead designer on Path of Exile and co-founder of Grinding Gear Games, discussed the merits of Larian's approach with Destin on YouTube. "A like Baldur's Gate 3 is a great example of a very true game," he says.

According to recent reports, "They made it, they had a good extended early access period for getting feedback without spoiling the game, and they released it in a sincere way," he explains. "Then, when given the opportunity to do more stuff for it, they mentioned, actually, we want to make something else. That's cool, they'll make another thing, and that'll do well.".

To his perception, "there's no manipulation there." Larian "got rewarded" appropriately and "everyone had a good time" in that transaction. "Sure, it's because it's an exceptionally good game," he adds. "But I think that a shift back to making games [like that] - it's less complicated, you can make more story-driven games. It doesn't have to be that everything is a live-service.".

According to recent reports, that's the million-dollar principle, really. Many games at the triple-A level simply don't need these features or mechanics, and Baldur's Gate 3 proves you can still have a close-to-one-to-one transaction between you and the player and be hugely successful.

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 and the Final Fantasy 7 remake trilogy are further examples. Wilson admits he probably wouldn't have made Path of Exile if they couldn't do it with live-service aspects, but that's because they were integral to the vision.

Sources indicate that "It's designed around a substantial economy with lots of players, which is why it's free-to-play," he states. "It was very much designed to be live-service from the start.".

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

The current problem is games are being released with online elements "because the spreadsheet says it'll make more money," and the game is "contorted out of its single-player true experience" to facilitate these elements.

It must be mentioned, it is refreshing still to play something and not have any online components to worry about or consider. Some games should just be their own experiences, and we need more of them - even if my to-play pile continues growing.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Pinball remains such an intoxicating game because it's one where you have to constantly be on your toes.
  • Especially considering the semi-realistic sci-fi vibe of it all.
  • At its most basic function, Appulse works exactly as you'd expect from a pinball game, in that you shoot your ball, or ship in this case, and hit those flappers to keep it in the air, so to speak.

Pinball remains such an intoxicating game because it's one where you have to constantly be on your toes. As the tiny metal sphere bats about the place, it's down to you to hit it at just the right time so as to keep racking up points upon points. It's a game of skill as much as it is luck. It is also incredibly silly, which is why I'm so tickled by Appulse, a sci-fi pinball roguelite top-down shooter that rolled out today wherein your ball is actually the main defence system on your spaceship.

According to recent reports, yes! This is also silly! Especially considering the semi-realistic sci-fi vibe of it all. It encourages me to wonder who in this world looked at pinball and thought, "yes, this is the optimum method of defending our ship from invading robots." And I love this fictional character for such a thought!

At its most basic function, Appulse works exactly as you'd expect from a pinball game, in that you shoot your ball, or ship in this case, and hit those flappers to keep it in the air, so to speak. Accept the key difference is your ball/ship has guns that you use to shoot the aforementioned invading robots, while also doubling up as an extra method for control. Need to right a bad hit? Shoot your shot and you'll fly off in the opposite direction.

According to recent reports, I've seen this in other digital pinball games before, but that's not a knock, I can't imagine having to manage all this shooting without some semblance of control. The roguelite mechanics sound pretty nifty too. You can get perks like extra recoil when firing, which obviously will aid you in staying in control. Or you may unlock the ability to slow down time. Builds sound pretty flexible! And overall it just looks like a neat little time. If Appulse takes your fancy, then as mentioned it's available to pick up on Steam now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that “Cancer does change you,” Kate Middleton indicates, emotion clear in her voice. “It changes your body, it changes you physically. But there’s a much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you.” These words come not at as an Instagram post or at a public event. Instead, they're the voice-over in a previously unannounced documentary about the Princess of Wales and her life since she disclosed a diagnosis of cancer in 2024.

According to Kensington Palace, which announced the film on Saturday, Heal is “a deeply personal upcoming documentary from The Princess of Wales, exploring life beyond diagnosis and the many ways people find comfort, strength and hope in the face of serious illness.” It will air on the BBC in the UK on November 29, and in the US on NBCUniversal on November 30.

Industry observers note that heal follows Kate Middleton during her participation in one of the United Kingdom’s most demanding endurance events: The National Three Peaks Challenge, which she completed this summer. In less than 24 hours, the princess climbed the three highest mountains in Scotland, England, and Wales: Ben Nevis (4,413 feet), Scafell Pike (3,209 feet), and Yr Wyddfa–Snowdon (3,559 feet). The undertaking wasn't just a personal effort, as it was also in support of the Royal Marsden Cancer Charity, an organization that supports people living with cancer before, during, and after the disease.

The documentary will also support that organization, Kensington Palace notes, saying “All funds received through the documentary's distribution have been directed to The Royal Marsden Cancer Charity to help people living with and beyond cancer.” The Royal Marsden Hospital, at which Middleton received treatment, is also referenced in the film, as Middleton's brother, James, asks her “Isn’t it when you leave the Royal Marsden, you ring the bell?”.

But while many patients participate in the bell-ringing ritual at the conclusion of treatment, Middleton says she missed out on that moment. “Yeah, but I didn’t ring the bell,” she replies. “So maybe this is your ringing of the bell,” James responded, suggesting her Three Peaks experience was that symbolic peal.

While Prince William is no stranger to documentary work, nor are Prince Harry and wife Meghan Markle, this is Kate Middleton's first venture into the format. Perhaps to ease her into the project, Heal's Director of Photography is a face quite familiar to the Princess: Will Warr, the filmmaker behind her video announcement marking the end of her chemotherapy treatments.

“Through this documentary, The Princess hopes to help others navigate diagnosis, recovery and life beyond cancer and transform access to holistic cancer care which supports wellbeing, resilience and quality of life during and after diagnosis,” Kensington Palace says of Heal, a message underscored by Middleton's words in the trailer. “You know, healing is a journey. How to reconnect with the things you once knew and how to find a sense of hope and joy alongside uncertainty.”.

Sources indicate that “It’s clear we're not meant to face life’s challenges alone,” the princess claims as the trailer concludes. “Things can renew and grow. Often it is through pain that we realize that there is a greater beauty that lies beyond that.".

Recent findings suggest that maths is not my strong suit, I make no secret of this, so when I come face to face with something like sudoku I will admit to recoiling in fear at having to confront this issue. Numbers don't make sense to me at the best of times, and now I have to figure out the specific placements of them whereby each number can only be used once per section, and each column and row have to all contain numbers one through nine? Terrifying! No, thanks, I'd much rather do the exact same thing but with, I don't know, skeletons and ghouls and the like. Which, conveniently, is more or less what Dungoku offers, a genre mashup of dungeon crawling and sudoku with a retro dark fantasy vibe.

Okay, it's not exactly the same. You don't crawl the dungeons in the typical fashion here as it leans heavily towards the puzzle side of things. Maps come in different, grid-based shapes and sizes, but to start they are mostly void of enemies. It's predominantly up to you to place enemies, or sometimes chests, in specific squares, all of which have their own rules that you must follow, with a set number that need to be placed on the map.

For example, one enemy may have a requirement that it is adjacent to a zombie in the same room. Another might need to be placed in a dead end. Others, like an owl creature, can only share a room with itself or other animals. So, it's different from sudoku in that each puzzle features changing enemies that have to be placed, as opposed to always needing to follow the same basic rules. It seems like a clever spin on the classic puzzle! Plus there's loot to be acquired that improves your stats and thereby your chance of survival (making a mistake in placement results in, obviously, getting hurt; this is still a dungeon crawler!).

In total there's apparently over 100 "hand-crafted dungeons to explore," and more than 20 monsters to take on, so it sounds like there's some good potential for interesting puzzle combinations. I also like the specific mention of "human composed music," certainly makes it sound like AI wasn't involved, and lord almighty I hope that to be true! No release date attached to this one just yet, but you can wishlist it on Steam in the meantime.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • EA Sports FC 27 is using gen-AI to digitally recreate the voice of veteran football commentator John Motson - the FIFA video game series' first ever real-world announcer who died in 2023.
  • In a recent development, john Motson commentated on hundreds of football games over the course of five different decades, starting in the 1970s.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EA Sports FC 27 is using gen-AI to digitally recreate the voice of veteran football commentator John Motson - the FIFA video game series' first ever real-world announcer who died in 2023.

In a recent development, john Motson commentated on hundreds of football games over the course of five different decades, starting in the 1970s. The English commentator then became the mainstay voice of EA's dominant football simulation series, beginning with FIFA 96 all the way up until FIFA 2005, when the publisher decided to go in a different direction.

According to recent reports, but EA's now decided to digitally resurrect Motson - or, at least, his incredibly recognisable voice - with permission from his family. An update with Motson's voice will go live on 26th November. "There was no way we would have moved forward with this in any way, shape or form if they weren't fully on board," senior game designer director Mat Prior remarked in a statement given to the BBC earlier today.

"At the outset we wanted to pay tribute to to Motty as the commentator and as this emotional connection - he was the very first voice of our game - so we really wanted to do him justice and bring him back," Prior added, explaining that Motson's posthumous role in the game is being handled with a mixture of previously recorded voice lines and AI. EA supposedly went down the AI route since it doesn't have recordings of Motson commentating over newer, more fresh faced footballers.

According to recent reports, fred Motson mentioned it "means an awful lot" to hear his dad's voice in the game again, and he reckons his dad was "always really keen to get involved in these kinds of projects," even if he wasn't the most technologically savvy person. EA said it had paid the family for the rights to use Motson's voice and likeness.

In a recent development, save Our Voices Now founder Peter Caulfield - who campaigns for the government to regulate the use of generative AI voice cloning tech - told the BBC he wasn't comfortable with the project. "In life or in death, unless you have specifically agreed to it, AI cloning of any kind should not be allowed," he mentioned. "Being a family member shouldn't automatically give you that right either." He doesn't have a problem with actors consenting to AI voice replication while they're still alive, however.

A Japanese acting union recently fought back against this very same practice by proposing new guidelines that would stop the replication of dead actors' voices without their permission.

Generative AI has been widely controversial in the games industry for other reasons, too. In recent months, there's been a huge impact on smaller game developers who are worried that their games could be cloned by AI copycats and some who have had to delay their release dates because of Steam's growing approvals backlog.

Industry observers note that "The Grounds comes across as a frippery, Ultimate Team rumbles ever on, but FC 27 brings meaningful changes to the fluidity and speed of play. Given that its practical football-game monopoly is more or less unchallenged, EA could do a lot less than this," Josh Wise wrote in Eurogamer's EA Sports FC 27 review.

Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando on February 01, 2026.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, I’ve got to be honest.
  • It’s still hard to believe that a Nor’easter came in and postponed the parade for the first time in its 100-year history (it has previously been outright canceled), and did so on the actual 100th anniversary.
  • On Thanksgiving, NBC has opted to just throw on last year’s 99th Annual Macy’s Day Thanksgiving Parade at 8:30 a.m.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, I’ve got to be honest. I was NOT dreaming of a white Thanksgiving this week, but that’s what people in many parts of the country got. If you got up this morning wondering how to watch the 100th Annual Macy’s Day Thanksgiving Parade, you may have gotten a rude awakening: It’s not hitting the 2026 TV schedule until Saturday. NBC does have a Turkey Day solution, but honestly, it’s not the one people on the Internet want.

I’m right there with them. It’s still hard to believe that a Nor’easter came in and postponed the parade for the first time in its 100-year history (it has previously been outright canceled), and did so on the actual 100th anniversary. Not even from like, snow. It seems like strong winds made the whole balloon part of the parade impossible. That’s crazy bad luck. However, NBC isn’t sitting on its laurels (and neither is Jimmy Fallon). Here’s what’s happening.

On Thanksgiving, NBC has opted to just throw on last year’s 99th Annual Macy’s Day Thanksgiving Parade at 8:30 a.m. in all time zones. NBC may have 99 problems, but no parade ain’t one. It’s not a bad idea really. The big balloons, c-list singers, and jazzy dance breaks are usually something most of us have on in the background anyway on this auspicious day. But social media users have a way better idea.

A slew of social media users think the better play would be to throw on a really old Macy’s Day Parade instead of last year’s. One user on X put it perfectly:.

I don't know who needs to hear this, but there are full length recordings of Macy's Thanksgiving Day parades from the '90s, with all the commercials, on YouTube.

They later joked the lineup from 2003 “looked pretty good.” Another user had a specific year request, too, writing:.

If they were smart they would air one from, like, 1991 in full.

This isn't the first Macy's Day Parade controversy this season. If you'd rather go the nostalgia play, another X user even noted you can throw one of these old episodes on via YouTube, and I thank this individual for that hot tip.

If you’re missing the Macys Thanksgiving Day Parade this morning you can find recordings of pretty much any year you want on YouTube. We pick a year and watch it every year mainly from the 90s before it turned into some weird rap event. 😂This year we are watching 1994.

In a recent development, it seems as if NBC’s strategy is the network doesn't want viewers to notice the parade is old, but there will be moments anyone actually paying attention to the broadcast should notice. I’m not saying that’s the world’s worst strategy given I already established a lot of us watch this while doing other tasks. Still, I think just going full in and putting on an older broadcast would be really fun, and I think would inspire people to pay closer attention and see what cultural references from the time are mentioned and what’s changed in the decades since.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Sources indicate that it’s a great idea, and now I just wish it was happening. Meanwhile, I’m still bummed I’ll have to wait a few more days to see Earl the Squirrel blown up in Epic proportion. Luckily, the Macy’s No-Longer-On-Thanksgiving Day Parade will make its triumphant return to NBC this Saturday. Happy 100th, y’all.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Action game maestro Hideki Kamiya really wants to make a new Castlevania game with publisher Konami.
  • The long-time developer best known for his work in the director's chair on a host of beloved games - Bayonetta, Resident Evil 2, Okami, Devil May Cry and The Wonderful 101 included - recently published a latest video to his personal YouTube account.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Action game maestro Hideki Kamiya really wants to make a new Castlevania game with publisher Konami.

The long-time developer best known for his work in the director's chair on a host of beloved games - Bayonetta, Resident Evil 2, Okami, Devil May Cry and The Wonderful 101 included - recently published a latest video to his personal YouTube account. While the video was first recorded last year, it does give us some hints on what Kamiya is interested in making after his in-development Okami sequel wraps up.

Perhaps the most noteworthy tidbit came from Kamiya advocating to make a fresh game in Konami's vampiric action-adventure series. "We'll definitely make Castlevania. If you let us work on it, we can make something truly insane, so just contact us and we'll be at your service," Kamiya remarked. (Thanks, Automaton!).

Kamiya presumably has his hands full with Capcom's Okami 2, which is right now in production at the director's newfound independent studio Clovers. Needless to say, any potential Kamiya-led Castlevania game will likely need to wait in a coffin for a while more.

In the meantime, it's not like Castlevania has remained dormant and defanged. Earlier this year, Konami promised that "numerous latest products around Castlevania" are in the pipeline. While new games weren't explicitly confirmed, it's safe to assume Konami would be interested in hearing pitches from outside devs. Kamiya can stay hopeful knowing that Evil Empire just dropped another gorgeous, aggressive action-platformer in the series.

"Like Rose herself, the game is earnest, intelligent, and capable of brilliance. But, mimicking its protagonist, it is also awkward, and unable to fully come to terms with its own unique identity in the shadow of its over-bearing legacy," Dom wrote in Eurogamer's Castlevania: Belmont's Curse review. "By no means is Belmont's Curse a bad game, I just think Evil Empire sunk its teeth a bit too deep into something it wasn't quite ready to consume.".

This isn't the first time Kamiya has publicly expressed interest in reviving older games, either. He recently remarked he's "100% serious" about bringing back Scalebound, his cancelled Xbox One exclusive.

1. Check your motherboard's SSD sockets/ports first.

2. Get the largest capacity SSD you can afford.

Industry observers note that 3. Get yourself a Gen4 (PCIe 4.0) NVMe SSD.

Industry observers note that 4. DRAM-less SSDs are perfectly fine for gaming.

Industry observers note that 5. Check your motherboard to see if you need an SSD with a pre-fitted heatsink.

Industry observers note that black Friday officially starts on Friday, November 27, but the deals tend to start rolling in a few days before that. Black Friday doesn't end until November 30, when we roll into even more online deals through Cyber Monday.

It's easy to get carried away at this time of year, but if you know how much you want to spend and what sort of SSD you're after, you'll be in good stead.

Industry observers note that capacity is a good starting point. At the moment, we're looking at some excellent 1 TB, 2 TB and 4 TB offers. A 512 GB SSD could still afford you a lot of speedy storage for a boot drive, with enough space for a handful of games, depending on the size, but this capacity is very slim nowadays. With memory supply crisis prices though, 512 GB isn't really the best value proposition anymore though.

Industry observers note that then think about the interface. Chances are, if you've been rocking a PC for the last five years, you'll have an M.2 slot in your motherboard with NVMe support. However, it's worth digging into the specifics of your motherboard to ensure it can support booting from such drives as not all can. Check out the manufacturer's pages and maybe forums too.

According to recent reports, it's also worth thinking about which version of the PCIe interface your storage slots operate on. On the AMD side, from the Ryzen 3000-series and up you should expect to have PCIe 4.0 slots on your motherboard, and from Intel's 11th-Gen Rocket Lake chips the same should be true. PCIe 4.0 drives are the more mainstream option today, which are widely supported. The faster PCIe 5.0 standard is pretty pricey and not necessarily worth it for gamers.

Industry observers note that there are some things to look out for, however. Some budget PCIe 3.0 drives only operate at x2 speed, which means they're half as fast as the standard x4 NVMe SSDs. These are pretty rare nowadays but it's worth double checking. It's also worth ensuring your M.2 SSD is an NVMe drive. There are some M.2 SSDs that still operate over the SATA interface and can only reach a maximum theoretical speed of 600 MB/s, while even a PCIe 4.0 drive can hit over 7,000 MB/s.

Sources indicate that there are always reasons to hold off on making a new purchase whenever you are thinking about making one. Whether it's the potential for a new generation of techie goodness on the horizon—either cutting prices on existing models or delivering tangible higher performance—or because there might be an imminent sale looming.

Recent findings suggest that when picking out SSD deals we take all of this into consideration, and where we think prices on something might significantly drop on the big day itself we simply won't recommend it. But all of the products here we either believe won't significantly drop much further in terms of their pricing, or are just good deals that we wouldn't hesitate recommending if you wanted to make a purchase today.

Industry News: Gemini's Fresh AI Agent Is Surprisingly Useful (If You Use Google for Everything)

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (828 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, google loves a rebrand.
  • Industry observers note that to use Task, open Gemini and create a upcoming chat.
  • According to recent reports, of course, I did the thing that every AI demo wants you to do: I asked Gemini to create a daily morning briefing for me, highlighting all important emails, calendar appointments, and tasks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, google loves a rebrand. What started off as "Spark" is now "Task" in Gemini—not to be confused with Google Tasks, the to-do app. Google took its Spark AI agent, which used to live in a separate tab, and integrated it into the Gemini interface. Gemini Task is available globally, and it’s completely free to use for some. That said, some features are limited to the U.S. and, of course, subject to some pretty strict usage limits. While not exactly a replacement for ChatGPT Dots or Meta Muse, you can think of Gemini Task as a controlled version of an AI agent that can do quite a lot in the background.

Industry observers note that to use Task, open Gemini and create a upcoming chat. You’ll see a Task tab next to Chat. Switch to it, and start writing your prompt. (You’ll also see some suggested options here.) Type your task or action and press "Send." The feature works best if you’ve already enabled Personal Intelligence on your Google account, and have connected services like Gmail, Google Drive, and Photos as well. You can then tag “@Gmail” to use your Gmail account, or even a third-party connector. Task natively supports automation, so you can say something like, "run this task once every day," and the AI will add it to your Scheduled Tasks section.

According to recent reports, of course, I did the thing that every AI demo wants you to do: I asked Gemini to create a daily morning briefing for me, highlighting all important emails, calendar appointments, and tasks. And, in my experience, it works really well. It reminded me of this article's due date, that I have a couple of pitches in my inbox to review, that a credit card bill is due soon, and that there are some holidays around the corner.

It has been revealed that gemini is very good at retrieving information from emails and taking action. For example, I created an automation that collects all my coffee orders for the month and presents the data in Google Sheets. I then asked Task to create a subscription manager for me. Instead of paying for a third-party app, it took a few minutes to collate the services I pay for into one list. It even accounted for the currency differences (some subscriptions are in USD, some in INR) and gave me a tally in INR, along with things like average monthly cost, and more.

While Gemini can connect to the open web, it's quite a hostile place right now for an AI bot. Websites are blocking agents from accessing their pages, which hinders their effectiveness. I asked Gemini to create a task that monitors the price of the Sony WH-1000XM5 headphones daily. For this, it asked my permission to spin up a remote browser, and loaded up Amazon, only to be blocked instantly. It did succeed in opening Croma though (a national retailer in India), but it took almost a minute for it to figure out that the price had not dropped below what I asked for. Would it be quicker and less resource-intensive if I did this myself? Yes, but the fact that Gemini can do this every evening like clockwork is the real advantage—as long as the websites comply, that is.

If you're going to try Task in Gemini for free, there are some limitations you should know about. The free plan only lets you run tasks once per day, and you can’t be granular about the exact timing. (Paid Gemini prepares have no such restrictions.) You can only run 10 tasks at the same time, while the limit is 50 tasks for AI Pro customers. Compute-based usage limits will also apply, based on your plan. The free access is currently live in India, the U.S., Canada, Australia, Japan, and South Korea.

Some features, though, are only for U.S. consumers. Gemini’s feature that lets you call businesses on your behalf is restricted to the States, as is the ability to forward emails to [email protected] to automatically turn the contents of the email into a task (like adding a college schedule to your calendar). U.S. users can also connect their Google Wallet account to set up payments at supported stores.

Gemini Task is not a proactive agent, nor is it trying to be. You still have to check the work. You have to approve any key steps, and if a website blocks AI models, there’s not a lot Gemini can do about it. For someone like me, who’s all-in on the Google ecosystem, I do see value in Gemini Task. The deep and robust Gmail integration is worth it alone. If you’re on the free blueprint, set up a couple of background tasks related to Gmail, Google Drive, or background research that run every morning, and call it a day. And if you’re paying for AI Pro, you can get a lot more done.

The Fable reboot had to look beyond Lionhead's RPG trilogy because games like The Witcher 3 "became the gold standard"

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Developer Playground Games had to look beyond Lionhead's original run of Fable games when rebooting the classic fantasy series, and it's all thanks to games like The Witcher 3, which changed what many players expect from their big RPGs and set a new "gold standard.".
  • The upcoming Fable reboot is finally ending its decade-long development journey soon.
  • Asked about what's changed during that time, in an interview with GamesIndustry.biz, studio founder and general manager Ralph Fulton named technological advancements as a biggie, but the impact of other games was perhaps even greater.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Developer Playground Games had to look beyond Lionhead's original run of Fable games when rebooting the classic fantasy series, and it's all thanks to games like The Witcher 3, which changed what many players expect from their big RPGs and set a new "gold standard.".

The upcoming Fable reboot is finally ending its decade-long development journey soon. Playground Games had to set up an entirely new team to work on its fairytale revival, so Fable's production wasn't quite as smooth sailing as the studio's consistently excellent Forza Horizon series, for example.

Asked about what's changed during that time, in an interview with GamesIndustry.biz, studio founder and general manager Ralph Fulton named technological advancements as a biggie, but the impact of other games was perhaps even greater.

"In 2015, The Witcher 3 redefined what an open-world action RPG looks like and became the gold standard," Fulton said. "And after that bar was raised, the Assassin's Creed franchise changed into this more modern iteration with Origins, Odyssey, and Valhalla, and became like a quasi-RPG.".

Sources indicate that "All of these games continue to reset player expectations," he continued. Millions of players suddenly had certain expectations about what their big-budget, open-world role-playing games should look like. So, Playground couldn't pull inspiration from Fable and Fable alone.

"I think looking only to the original Fable trilogy for inspiration would leave us lacking in terms of what the modern audience, the modern marketplace, expects," Fulton added.

Still, Playground's Fable is drawing most heavily from Lionhead's Fable. Fulton specifically mentions the game's signature British wit and in-flux morality system as examples. Then there's also the spontaneous life sim elements that "none of our competitors do," according to Fulton. "It's a totally Fable thing, the social simulation and economic simulation. Okay, there are games that have economic simulations, but they're not in [our] RPG category. Fable is unique in that it's almost like a life sim in terms of genre.".

Raising four separate families and becoming the entire map's benevolent landlord was one of the funnest parts of Fable back in the day, alongside those sometimes silly characters. Seeing next year's Fable lean into those systemic choices, and having Albion's NPCs react to them more believably, could give this one a very long shelf life.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that it’s a balmy late-September day in London, and Dolly Alderton is explaining to a befuddled Emma Frost what “iPhone face” means. Frost has never heard the term; her fellow showrunners Alderton and Zoe Kazan have.

According to recent reports, “You know [how] you look at some faces, like Rosamund Pike’s face—it looks like it’s never seen an iPhone? It looks like it’s seen a lute and a loom,” Alderton tells Frost.

According to recent reports, “So actors who look like they’re comfortable in a period show, rather than feeling inherently modern,” states Frost, as understanding dawns. Alderton and Kazan affirm her: “Yes, yes. Exactly.”.

According to recent reports, now that Frost gets it, she turns back to the group’s Zoom screen. “Sorry, what was the question?”.

In a recent development, kazan began her career as an actor, while Alderton started out as a dating columnist and Frost was a sculptor and painter. Now all three are overseeing vastly different but comparable Netflix period dramas, each based on a classic work of literature: East of Eden (Kazan’s, which was released October 1), Pride and Prejudice (Alderton’s, out December 3), and The Age of Innocence (Frost’s, coming February 18). They’ve gathered in a London conference room at Netflix headquarters for a roundtable discussion about art, work, the unique experience of adapting a beloved book—and, apparently, iPhone face.

Industry observers note that though this is the first time the trio has met face to face, their conversation flows so easily and naturally that interrupting them with questions sometimes feels impolite. Early on, I note that all three of these novels are, on some level, about unconventional women. Alderton, Frost, and Kazan pause for a moment, considering this Lit 101–level observation.

“That’s true, I think,” agrees Frost.

And then they’re off to more interesting topics.

Vanity Fair: Have you read each other’s books?

Dolly Alderton: No, I haven’t read either of your books.

Alderton: Did you read them at school, or did you read them for fun?

Recent findings suggest that frost: Pride and Prejudice I read when I was a teenager at school. East of Eden I read first about 15 years ago, I think.

Alderton: So Em already wins the round table.

Frost: And for both of you, was it the thing you most wanted to adapt?

Sources indicate that alderton: I would never have dared to dream to. I was so overwhelmed when I was first approached. I just thought, it’s such a precious IP. It would be way too much, and I wouldn’t be the right person. But then when I was asked to pitch for it, at that point there’s no other answer but yes.

Kazan: First of all, was it the Austen you liked the most?

Alderton: Yes. It was the one that I’ve always loved because of Lizzie Bennet. I’ve always been obsessed with Lizzie Bennet. She was my hook. But how about you two? Did you ever dream of adapting these texts?

Recent findings suggest that frost: I was at a place where I mentioned, “I want to do anything except period, because I’ve done so much period.” Netflix asked me to do The Age of Innocence, and it was, I think at that moment, the one book that made me just go, “Oh my God, okay, let me go back and revisit it.” Because I know I love it, but you have to know what the reason is [to adapt it again]. And the thing that totally blew me away on a reread was how relevant and resonant it is. It is about the freedom of the individual versus the conformity of the pack. It has so many themes in it that are really resonant with social media, the bullying of the group.

It has been revealed that alderton [turning to Kazan]: Tackling Cathy, how did you begin? What was your way into that?

Kazan: I think of adaptation as an advanced form of reading. For me, everything I’ve ever written has come from a feeling of “I have to write this specific thing.” When I was 15 and I read the book for the first time, I felt like it literally grabbed me by the throat and wouldn’t let go. And then I just kept coming back to it. And specifically her character, I felt like I had never read anyone like that before or since.

[to Alderton] The BBC’s Pride and Prejudice—is that the one that you—.

Alderton: No, that wasn’t my Pride and Prejudice.

According to recent reports, alderton: Yeah, the Joe Wright one was the one that I was more familiar with. But I’m so interested in what you were saying about getting to know Cathy. I was kind of nervous about doing press for a book that’s so beloved, and I’m finding it’s actually been really easy so far because I just know the people so well. So much of it has been basically like, putting Mr. Darcy and Elizabeth, all the Bennet family and Bingley through therapy. That psychological interrogation of these very well-known characters has been the thing I’ve just really, really enjoyed.

Frost: Have you both had to change points of view from the novel? Do you feel like you’ve had to make a specific choice about who you are foregrounding? I think I know the answer in your case, Zoe.

Recent findings suggest that kazan: No, I actually don’t. I’m aware that the way that I read a book is different from the way that anyone else reads that book. When I read East of Eden, I feel like I see Steinbeck becoming enthralled by this character, finding her as curious as I do. I think he starts out a real place of judgment and over the course of the book, really moves towards love and understanding.

Sources indicate that alderton: I have a similar thing in that for the majority of the book, one of the lead characters is completely unknowable. Not just to Elizabeth, but to the audience as well. So you have to honor that to make it satisfying. That’s kind of frustrating when you’re writing a romantic lead for the first three and a half episodes. None of us, least of all the female protagonist, can see who he is, and we misunderstand him. There is no other option I think than staying with Lizzie.

Frost: It’s very different because the book is entirely from Newland’s point of view. The thing that I wanted to do, and that Netflix were really excited for me to do, was to open it up to find out who the women were.

According to recent reports, I think in the book—rightly, because she’s writing from Newland’s point of view—both May and Ellen are sort of constructed as his other. One is the thing to be won, and one is effectively the antagonist. It’s so interesting, because it’s a female author—and [Wharton herself], she’s part Newland. That's who she was growing up. And she’s part Ellen, this woman who now lives in Europe, who's become really cosmopolitan, who is even based on her own love triangle.

It has been revealed that the impossibility of that love triangle is the thing I want people to feel. It’s not like one of them is wrong. They're all just feeling what they’re feeling.

Alderton: And how do you feel about bringing that upcoming perspective and analysis to the story? For a book that's so beloved, did you feel excited by that? Or did you feel kind of daunted by it?

Frost: Maybe I should have felt daunted. I didn’t. I think Edith Wharton—it’s so based on her own personal experience of when she was 45, she had this sexual awakening. She was in this really dull marriage. She’d never had an orgasm. When she was 45, she fell in love with this journalist and had this passionate affair.

It has been revealed that frost: She had this massive affair, then he ghosted her. But she was trying to make sense of it through this love triangle. When she wrote it, she couldn’t possibly have written herself as a female character in the center of an illicit love triangle because we were still in time of censorship, and she was being published in a very commercial magazine. So she had to make herself the man that has more agency.

Alderton: With any script, you have a relationship with the characters. But with what we are doing, you have this relationship with the writer.

Kazan to Alderton: You’re also a novelist. How are you thinking about bisecting yourself—using both parts of your brain, the novelist part and the dramatist part?

According to recent reports, alderton: I’ll tell you how I felt about it. I’ve written two novels, both of which I’ve tried to adapt. I found it really, really hard. I found adapting Pride and Prejudice incredibly effortless. When I went from Pride and Prejudice to my novel, I was like, "Why is this so much harder? I hate this novelist. Jane Austen is so much easier.".

Recent findings suggest that what amazed me is just, it’s like she wrote it to be adapted. Recent findings suggest that the Challenge alum Nicole Zanatta welcomed twin daughters Seraphina and Madyson on May 1. “Becoming their mom has been the greatest blessing of my life, but our journey hasn’t been easy,” Zanatta wrote via Instagram on June 1. “Both of my girls were diagnosed with congenital CMV (Cytomegalovirus), a virus I had never heard of until it became part of our story.” She continued, “Since birth, we’ve spent time in the NICU, attended countless appointments which are still ongoing, undergone testing and started medications. I recently brought them home a week ago, but our journey is far from over. Through every high and low, I choose faith over fear, resilience over doubt, and gratitude for every blessing along the way. I will give my girls every opportunity to thrive. I will always fight for them and advocate for their needs.” According to the Mayo Clinic, CMV is "a condition caused by a common virus.” The CMV virus stays in the body for life once a person is infected and can spread through body fluids, including blood, saliva, urine, semen and breast milk.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Despite the far higher prices of PlayStation and Xbox consoles today compared to their launch, or even the same period last year, both brands of console saw a significant boost in US sales leading up to the launch of this generation's biggest game: Grand Theft Auto 6.

In the week ending 14th November, PS5 hardware unit sales registered a 2.4x increase over the same week last year. Xbox wasn't far behind, seeing a 2.3x increase in its own unit sales. That's according to industry analyst Mat Piscatella at Circana, who pulled the data from Circana's retail tracking service, which covers the US retail market.

The PS5 Pro only accounted for less than 10 percent of the PlayStation's total unit sales, by the way, which Piscatella noted was "a LOT better than it has been in recent weeks", and seemingly the result of increased supply.

GTA 6, of course, released on 19th November, so the surge in console hardware sales was clearly driven by the rush to attain consoles before the game came out. And while the GTA 6-driven demand isn't surprising, it's worth noting how much more expensive PS5 and Xbox Series X/S consoles are today.

Sources indicate that A standard PS5 today costs $650, compared to $550 a year ago. The PS5 Pro saw a big jump from $750 last November to $900 today. The base Xbox Series X jumped from $650 last year to $800 today, while Series S now costs $500, up from $400.

Even Switch 2, where GTA 6 is not available, saw a notable boost of 40 percent in hardware sales over the same period, driven by The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake and the special edition Zelda Switch 2 console.

It has been revealed that circana's November US video game market report, which releases in December, is already one of the most anticipated this year, for digesting and documenting the GTA 6 effect. Worldwide, GTA 6 sold more than 32.5m copies in one day, making Rockstar's parent manufacturer Take-Two $3.79bn (£2.89bn) in revenue. We haven't had any updated official sales figures since; but estimates suggest the sales figure could be well into the 40-millions. Perhaps Rockstar is waiting to hit the nice round 50m sales mark before announcing it.

If you're playing GTA 6, you may want to keep Eurogamer's GTA 6 walkthrough to hand. It has plenty of very helpful guides covering the game's main missions, as well as explainers for mechanics like romance and the criminal profile, and even cheats for when you finish the game.

We had a woman losing her pants, a theater kid repeatedly making vampire analogies. I could go on and on about all the vibrant personalities, but with only two episodes to go in the season, it’s now becoming clear Survivor 51 might be best remembered for something else: producing one of the most dominant winners ever.

In a recent development, there are seven castaways left on Survivor 51, and Sharonda is both the best connected player and the one who seems to be running the entire game. Fans have been all over her as the likely winner of the season for weeks, but this past episode in particular screamed her credentials from a helicopter in Fiji. She was given credit in very specific detail for engineering both of the last two votes, and as viewers, we’ve been told exactly where she stands with all the key players left in the game. I mean seriously, let’s just run down her relationships that have been spelled out explicitly.

Industry observers note that she’s in a secret pact with Jelly and Devin as part of the helicopter alliance. As an audience, we have been told about this secret group since the first episode, but the remaining players still have no idea what’s going on. That alliance is clearly the main story of the season, and she is right at the center of it.

Recent findings suggest that then there’s Cristian, who we have seen Sharonda repeatedly manipulate. First he told her about Carter’s idol, then she lied and convinced him to turn on Maggie. It was only at the end of this past episode, after he watched Carter walk out the door, that he finally realized she’s not his friend. Then there’s Eric, who she straight up mentioned she can get to do whatever she wants. I have to assume he feels the same way since he got no confessionals this week to rebut that.

According to recent reports, we saw some tension between her and Mike this week, as she advocated for Carter being eliminated and he advocated for Thien An being eliminated. I bet you can guess who won that substantial showdown. Carter went home, and Mike ultimately voted with Sharonda, despite the fact that he had a final two alliance with the loveable farmer. Maybe he’ll give us a confessional next week where he explains why he went down that path, but from the perspective of the audience, it looks like she just barrelled over him and got her way.

Ordinarily, when Survivor shows us a player looking this dominant this early in the game, it’s a bad sign. It means everyone else is about to conspire to get them out because they’re such an obvious threat to win the game that they have to be eliminated. Maybe that’s what we’ll see with Sharonda, but I’m not so sure that’s going to happen this season. We’re not getting confessionals from other players about how she needs to be taken out, and there aren’t actually many people left in the game who the edit is telling us can win.

Seriously, who else can win this game right now? Jelly is definitely the other most likely contender. She’s gotten a main character edit, and we’ve heard castaways talk about how she’s a threat to win the game, but she got two total confessionals this past episode and players have repeatedly talked about getting her out during their confessionals. Devin still has an outside shot I guess. He’s this season’s leader in confessionals, but the edit has also repeatedly dunked on him for all the mistakes he has made.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

That goes double for Mike. We’ve gotten his perspective pretty consistently, but we’ve also heard a ton from other players about how much they don’t like him. He's possible but very, very unlikely. Eric is a wacky side character who seems like a zero vote finalist. Cristian had two confessionals in the first four episodes combined and Thien An is the most underedited player in the entire season who we’re repeatedly told has no allies. According to recent reports, I’m not saying Sharonda is for sure going to win Survivor 51, but if she does win Survivor 51, she is probably going to be remembered as one of the most dominant winners ever. She hasn’t had a single vote cast against her, and she’s voted correctly in every single tribal council so far, except the one where Linnea went home and multiple advantages were played. In a recent development, if Sharonda wins, it is going to look dominant, and we’re going to be talking about her in the same way we do Tony, Kim and other legends who gave us a masterclass. There’s still a long way to go, but at this point, I think it’s better than 50-50 it happens.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, in August 2025, Aeternum Game Studios unveiled that Aeterna Lucis, the sequel to the well-liked 2021 metroidvania Aeterna Noctis, would be delayed from its planned launch in September of that year to sometime in 2026, for one good reason: Silksong. Just prior to that, Team Cherry surprised everyone by announcing that the Hollow Knight: Silksong launch was imminent, and Aeternum—and a whole bunch of others—decided the smart move was to just get out of the way.

In a recent development, well, here we go again. Yesterday, Team Cherry announced that "Cherry Time" is coming on November 27, with "a bunch of exciting announcements, plus an update on Hollow Knight: Silksong - Sea of Sorrow," the Silksong expansion announced in December 2025. Some fans are hoping that means the Sea of Sorrow release date will be announced—or maybe even that it will actually be released.

Whatever's coming, Aeternum says that this time around, it's standing firm.

Sources indicate that "Dear Team Cherry," Aeternum wrote in an Official Statement: Part 2 message, riffing on the "Official Statement" it put out in 2025. "A little over a year ago, just as we were about to launch our game, you announced Silksong. We stepped aside, pushed the whole project back a year, and, honestly, it was one of the best decisions we've ever made: The genre had an incredible year, and we got to enjoy Silksong as fans and polish Aeterna Lucis into the game we always dreamed it would be.

"Now here we are again, just days from launch. Aeterna Lucis, our newly introduced Metroidvania, comes out on December 3... and you announce Cherry Time.

"This time we're staying put. Not to go against you, but because a lot of people have been waiting for the Queen of Light for a long time, and we don't want to make them wait any longer.".

Official statement, part II. Here we go again….

Sources indicate that you might say that there's some element of opportunism at work here. Aeterna Lucis launches on December 3, one week from today, and since that's surely way too close for another delay (not to mention it was pushed back a year already), the next-best option is to leverage this new Silksong moment in whatever way possible.

Keep up to date with the most key stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Still, it's hard not to have sympathy for Aeternum. Maybe this Cherry Time announcement won't be a substantial deal, but then again, maybe it will be a very big deal. Aeternum is being a good sport about it, but I have to think there's some real frustration behind its message.

Industry observers note that and with good reason. This isn't a situation like Devolver Digital launching Volvy alongside GTA 6—that is, two completely different games with virtually no meaningful audience overlap. Aeterna Lucis and Hollow Knight: Silksong are both fantasy metroidvanias, and there's a lot of potential crossover there. If Team Cherry does unload Sea of Sorrow before the end of the year, that could—almost certainly will— cut deeply into Aeterna Lucis.

In a recent development, "We have to ask, with all the love in the world: Is it just us, or does the universe have it in for us? Hahaha. And since you're about to wreck our lives all over again, the least we can do is make a bundle together.".

Hey, you can't blame 'em for taking a shot, especially under the circumstances. "Hahaha," indeed.

It has been revealed that aeterna Lucis launches on Steam on December 3. Cherry Team, whatever it turns out to be, will kick off at 10 am ET/1 pm PT on November 27.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that many World of Warcraft: Forever players are at the moment in the midst of a substantial PvP reputation grind.
  • In a recent development, the battleground in question is Alterac Valley, a 40 person-a-side clash between Alliance and Horde factions, where both sides need to push their forces across a snowy, mountainous map into the opposing faction's base to take down the NPC General waiting there.
  • In a recent development, played the intended way, Alterac Valley is a lengthy battle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that many World of Warcraft: Forever players are at the moment in the midst of a substantial PvP reputation grind. However, this process has been disrupted due to a sudden change to one of the game's battleground PvP arenas.

In a recent development, the battleground in question is Alterac Valley, a 40 person-a-side clash between Alliance and Horde factions, where both sides need to push their forces across a snowy, mountainous map into the opposing faction's base to take down the NPC General waiting there. Alterac Valley is being grinded by max-level players for its gear rewards that are given once reaching "exalted" reputation there. At the moment it's some of the best gear available ahead of raids being introduced next month.

In a recent development, played the intended way, Alterac Valley is a lengthy battle. The Generals on both sides are fearsomely tough but by rushing to capture certain structures on the way to this battle, you can weaken the Generals enough to make them easier to overcome. As such, players have been fast-tracking this PvP instance, skipping smaller objectives and rushing core objectives to get to the Generals as fast as possible. This bypassed a lot of the incidental skirmishing allure of Alterac Valley, but it was an efficient way to promptly gain reputation and Honor points (PvP currency).

But this strategy has been pretty much killed outright as of today. In a post made to the official World of Warcraft forums, community manager Kaivax revealed that the reputation gained from killing the Generals has been drastically reduced, while the reputation gained from killing other NPCs and capturing previously ignored objectives now grants more. Generals are also granted a buff that makes them incredibly strong for the first 20 minutes of a match, which is then reduced for each objective taken.

In a recent development, this is a good change in regard to the experience of playing Alterac Valley. While rushing through was good for players looking to gain reputation rapidly, they weren't really playing the Battleground in the way it's meant to be played. The dev post reads: "The overall intent for all of these changes was for games to feel more meaningful while trying to maintain a similar amount of rep gained over a similar playtime within the battleground, even with longer match lengths. There will be fluctuations depending on how successful you are at destroying towers and holding capture points at the end of a match however.".

According to recent reports, so how has the community reacted? Badly! Taking a gander at community hubs following this change shows plenty of frustration. Take this comment by Reddit user Athrek: "I'm fine with the changes if they give it Rank Points and calendar events. But they've gutted the rep for both sides, extended the time it takes to play, and it still gives zero Rank Points. Now you may as well get to the win condition and then sit there for a few hours, gaining the passive rep cause there's nothing else of value to be had.".

It has been revealed that it appears as of writing that the reputation gained isn't as much as it was previously, so those playing purely for reputation have been hit. There's another element of frustration which is that those who rushed to level 60 and ground Alterac Valley reputation and rewards before the changes won't be affected by this. Perhaps that's the allure of rushing to level 60!

Sources indicate that "This is why the WoW mantra is 'exploit early, exploit often'," writes user Lanienah12. "Some people are already exalted with AV rep and will receive no punishment for it; meanwhile upcoming people will be spending 3x as long." Especially in the wake of the Blackmaw Hold gold exploit being discovered by these frontrunners, there's a growing belief that those taking their time or that are limited by real-life factors are feeling the brunt of these changes.

As is often the case with major sales these days, retailers are increasingly blurring the lines between early deals and the official start of a sale. Black Friday sales have essentially become a month-long event, with early deals appearing in the first week of the month. If you haven't been paying attention, major retailers have already declared their prepares and started churning out deals. But you're still in time to make this Black Friday sale a great one. Here's everything you need to know about the big sale.

Black Friday is always the day after Thanksgiving. This year, Black Friday starts at midnight on Nov. 27. Cyber Monday is the Monday following Black Friday, which starts at midnight on Nov. 30.

The major retailers running sales are the usual ones: Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, Home Depot, and many others. Currently, Walmart has publicized its plans already and has early deals available. Best Buy is offering one of the largest Black Friday and Cyber Week sales, with multiple events and early deals. Target has a three-day event. Nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Cyber Monday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026.

Amazon Black Friday: November 19.

Best Buy Black Friday: November 19.

Walmart Black Friday: November 23.

Target Black Friday: November 27.

Black Friday used to be bigger for major retailers and more expensive tech and appliances, while Cyber Monday was better for cheaper tech and gave smaller businesses a chance to compete online. Nowadays, though, the distinction is almost meaningless. Every major retailer will offer sales on both days, and the smart move is to know what you want, do your research, or refer to guides like our Black Friday and Cyber Monday coverage that have done all the vetting for you.

In a recent development, unlike Spring or Summer sales, Black Friday doesn't focus on specific categories, which means everything is fair game for discounts. In previous years, we've seen tech, tools, fitness equipment, outdoor supplies and furniture, bedding, video games, kitchen appliances, and more. This is one of the best times to make a list of what you need. You're likely to find what you're looking for discounted, and probably at its lowest price it has ever been. If you'd like to avoid having to do all that work, we always vet all of our deals for you. Just follow our Black Friday coverage.

Black Friday sales officially begin Friday, November 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  November 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

Yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

In a recent development, nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

Yes. Walmart, Best Buy, Target, and Home Depot will all have in-store deals, some of which you might not find online, so if you're able to take a trip to your local retailer, keep your eyes open for different deals.

Of course, depending on what you're shopping for, you might find other opportunities throughout the year, but in general, Prime Day and Black Friday have the best sales.

Madison Square Garden Entertainment Corp. reportedly locked out its own security staff for the occasion, like it was a Mob bar—the kind with no windows. Not even members of the Newly introduced York Police Department were allowed their own phones on site.

In a recent development, love may be free, but the performance of it is not. It requires crates, trucks, officers on overtime, private jets, SUVs, HVACs, all the queen’s horses, all the queen’s men, a Jumbotron. Conspiracy theories do not tell you the truth, but they do tell a kind of psychological truth about a place or its people. Had The Star and Redwood filmed the ceremony, perhaps for theatrical release or streaming—maybe on Disney+, which paid The Star a king’s ransom for the rights to another project? (A person with knowledge claims the couple has no aims to drop a documentary about their big day.).

In a recent development, around the barricades of Madison Square Garden, in the wake left by The Star, her groom, and their guests, her fans gathered. Some had been there for hours, wanting to be nearer to their pious majesty. A white truck passed. Pastries—from the merrymaking gentry presumably, though who can say for certain—were distributed, with an assist from a cop in uniform and gear.

If you listened carefully then to the sounds of the city—not for any semantic meaning, but if you were to really pitch your ears to the utopic promise of music—you might have heard the determined whoosh of a weighted blade dropping, dropping, dropping, the ax of public opinion falling in downward demotic motion.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that ubisoft is clearly serious about implementing generative-AI deeply into the game development process.
  • That's according to a newly introduced Vertical Slice report, citing multiple anonymous sources at the moment working at Ubisoft.
  • Several employees said that pitching a game idea without gen-AI or without explaining why it does not involve the use of the controversial tech will not receive the greenlight.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that ubisoft is clearly serious about implementing generative-AI deeply into the game development process. The French publisher now expects teams pitching upcoming project ideas to be prepared to explain how gen-AI will help with developing the game.Teams who don't want to use gen-AI will need to clearly justify their reasoning to the higher-ups.

That's according to a newly introduced Vertical Slice report, citing multiple anonymous sources at the moment working at Ubisoft.

Several employees said that pitching a game idea without gen-AI or without explaining why it does not involve the use of the controversial tech will not receive the greenlight. This is especially relevant for smaller games with tight teams who now reportedly must deal with Ubisoft leaders' desire to implement gen-AI if they want to get their pitches reviewed.

Industry observers note that "We were told that using AI will increase the speed at which pitches can be made by 'small lean agile teams,'" one source remarked. "We were told that as the goal was to move fast, iterate and discard projects to sift out the good stuff. AI was essential in maintaining a rapid pace.".

Sources indicate that while some said Ubisoft is not openly mandating gen-AI use to staff, others feel "cornered" by gen-AI. One source said Ubisoft views the tech as "unavoidable", and that only a minority of the company's audience reject it.

Sources indicate that ubisoft recently gave name to an internal initiative to expand the use of generative-AI and research how its developers can make use of the technology. It's called Motherbrain, and it has its own division within Ubisoft.

Over a year ago, Ubisoft embarked on a major restructuring effort that has seen the formation of fresh subsidiaries, the consolidation of its biggest brands into 'creative houses', the closure of studios and, of course, multiple rounds of layoffs.

Recent findings suggest that "Ubisoft is in a top-down nightmare of AI psychosis," one source added, pointing to the already low morale within the company. "Yves [Guillemot] has hitched his wagon to the tech, demanding the rest of the company follow on.".

With confirmation that Pattinson is the new James Bond, I have a good feeling that he might also be the most interesting version of 007 yet. Here's why.

Recent findings suggest that while many people will likely say that Keaton is the best Batman, I think it's even more likely that most people will say that Sean Connery is the best Bond. Every subsequent Bond actor has unfortunately been judged against Connery, with many people saying that they liked Daniel Craig's bruiser Bond since he was a callback to the tough guy Bond that Connery represented.

It has been revealed that connery is also the reason why some people disregard Roger Moore's Bond, as some people think he verges too far into the silly territory. Personally, of all men who have played Bond, my favorite is Pierce Brosnan, but I respect those who prefer George Lazenby or Timothy Dalton.

That said, I think Robert Pattinson, who I've already gone on record calling my favorite modern actor, will probably provide the most interesting take on the character yet. When trying to envision him as Bond, I think of his roles in Tenet, The Batman, and Primetime, all rolled into one. I see him being a subtler, quieter Bond than others (maybe closest to Dalton), and I'm looking forward to him creating his own version far removed from anything like Connery. Can you tell that I'm excited?

We've had a James Bond who's been Remington Steele, a James Bond who was in The Golden Compass, a James Bond who was Indiana Jones’ dad, and a James Bond who was in Flash Gordon, but we've never had a James Bond who was ALSO Batman, and I just love that this is now going to be a reality.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

#143215. Breaking: Fed up of Steam's lack of action regarding AI slop? Maybe you should take a look at the 'Games Without AI' event, instead

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (773 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Eurogamer ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Fed up of Steam's lack of action regarding AI slop? Maybe you should take a look at the 'Games Without AI' event, instead

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (773 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that yesterday, a new Steam event went live that claims all games featured in it have avoided AI entirely during development.
  • Industry observers note that "Behind every game, there are people, ideas, passion, and countless hours of creative work," remarked a mission statement.
  • There are plenty of games featured in the event, and not just ones tied to the organisers, as the cynical-minded amongst you may expect.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that yesterday, a new Steam event went live that claims all games featured in it have avoided AI entirely during development. The event, called 'Games Without AI', has been set up by a third party rather than Valve - by Dev Land Marketing, All Ages Of Geek, and Dark Cocooning - to "support real creators" and runs from 25th November to 6th December.

Industry observers note that "Behind every game, there are people, ideas, passion, and countless hours of creative work," remarked a mission statement. "We've carefully curated a selection of independent games that celebrate human creativity, craftsmanship, and collaboration, all made without generative AI. But Games Without AI is more than a festival. It's also about bringing developers, players, and creators together to build a community where we share knowledge, support one another, and grow together.".

There are plenty of games featured in the event, and not just ones tied to the organisers, as the cynical-minded amongst you may expect. Ones that jump out to my eye are: Pidgeon Pocket, a 'cozy incremental' with pixel art and a flock of adorable pigeons that you need to upgrade; Bottled by Bears, which tasks you with collecting and discovering rare bees, bottling honey jars, and expanding your farm; and Arctic Awakening, which sort-of looks like Pacific Drive meets Subnautica, in the Arctic.

Industry observers note that the event was posted to Reddit where commenters immidiately began accusing certain games of having used AI in their development - often without proof. One user, however, who claims to have been a developer trying to submit a game for inclusion in the event, offered some insight on how the selection process worked.

Sources indicate that "As one of participants I can assure you that the qualification process was restrictive[ly] hard to bypass," they wrote. "We were all required to provide proofs of the game being made without AI and share as much of the process as possible. Then it was actually voted by community, which games are convicing enough so the whole process was intended to be as objective as possible. It's an event meant for developers who take pride in their games being made by humans so if any participant attends with ill intend of showing that AI generated game can get through... That would be very sad and shameful. From what I've seen, none of the selected games can be reasonable suspected of that. I also know some other participants personally and they are genuine zero-AI devs.".

Industry observers note that it's refreshing to see curation turned towards explicitly anti-AI games: between major publishers chasing the trend and smaller indie studios being caught out using the dubious tech, it's nice to see a library of games that promises that no AI was used during development. Given that Valve itself recently claimed it was up to developers themselves to ensure their games couldn't be ripped off by cheap AI tools, I'm happy to see an initiative rallying against the normalcy of all this.

The most recent Steam Next Fest had more than double the number of demos than last year, but that stat isn't what it seems on the surface: roughly 17 percent of those games listed the use of generative AI, but it seemed that many more games did not disclose the use of AI in their development. In June's event, more than a thousand games in Steam Next Fest featured a generative AI disclosure of some kind, which made up roughly 20 percent of all featured games.

Industry observers note that over the past 18 months or so, we've seen the issue of generative AI in games on Steam evolve quite a lot. AI tools have been used to clone games, resulting in a troubling trend of imitation games taking the spotlight away from real indie devs. Whilst Steam, as a storefront, has been steadfast in requiring games to declare their use of generative AI during development, there are loopholes: devs that claim they only use AI tools for "efficiency gains" can appear on the store without any declaration.

Recent findings suggest that at the other end of the spectrum is Epic Games' Tim Sweeney, who last year criticised Valve's requirement to disclose generative AI, saying, "Steam and all digital marketplaces need to drop the 'Made with AI' label. It doesn't matter any more." The swell of users rejecting AI in games, though, seems to run counter to that argument. Recently, Big Walk developer House House revealed it used generative AI "sparingly" during the development of the co-op darling, and received a lot of backlash online.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the United Video Game Workers-CWA union has released a report with details on the hardship fund it started in collaboration with Necrosoft Games earlier this year benefiting laid-off developers. The UVW reports that through its itch.io bundle and from monies received via union dues and outside donations, it raised $290,000 over two weeks. All that cash has been dispersed to over 150 devs from across the industry to help with expenses like rent, medical bills, and other debt.

"This came at a time when I deeply, deeply needed a hand to pull me up while I'm drowning.".

Thanks to your support, we were able to disburse $290K in funds to over 150 game workers facing hardship after unprecedented mass layoffs.

Here's what some recipients had to say: ð§µ.

— United Videogame Workers-CWA (@videogameworkers.bsky.social) 2026-11-24T00:58:08.876Z.

It has been revealed that perusing the report’s list of studios from which applicants to the fund have been laid off is depressing. Among them are some of the biggest names in the industry: Xbox, Activision Blizzard, EA, Ubisoft, and more. It’s the human reckoning, the terrible price to all the industry upheaval that’s often glossed over in reports on resets, booming financials, and robust pipelines. The other equally sad detail is just how long many of these out-of-work people have worked in the industry, with 32 percent of applicants reporting 10 years or more.

The industry is experiencing a brain drain that will be incredibly difficult to recover from. According to recent reports, is there a little bit of wink wink, nudge nudge to that 'not a Black Friday fest' business? Hey, maybe.

Recent findings suggest that in fair play, though, Steam traditionally hasn't run Black Friday sales, because its Autumn Sale was always happening at the same time. The realignment of seasonal sales in 2025 changed that, however, leaving a hole that was filled by the first-ever Steam Black Friday Sale last year.

Sources indicate that valve has other priorities this year, though, which could explain the absence (wink wink, nudge nudge) of an official Black Friday event on Steam in 2026. If it's treated like an 'almost a Steam sale' that never really ends, I have to think that developers and gamers alike will benefit—at least until we all get used to it and Valve has to figure out some newly introduced way to tweak the formula.

Sources indicate that and here's one other difference between actual Steam sales and the Black Friday non-event: Valve said the Black Friday decor will come off the Discounts and Events page on November 30, but the discounts themselves all have separate end dates. In a recent development, samsung’s flagship soundbars have reached the point where the yearly upgrades are more about refinement than reinvention, and that is pretty much the story with the Samsung HW-Q990H—and this 2026 model is on sale for $500 off for Black Friday, down to $1,497.99 from $1,997.99. That's its lowest price to date.

Samsung kept the same 11.1.4-channel setup from the older HW-Q990F, including the soundbar, wireless subwoofer, and two rear speakers, but leaned harder into software this time around—features like the SpaceFit Sound Pro automatically adjust the sound depending on your room layout, and unlike some auto-calibration features that barely change anything, this one reportedly shifts the audio balance in noticeable ways. Sometimes it improves dialogue clarity and bass response. Other times, you may prefer tweaking things yourself with the built-in seven-band EQ.

The system also handles basically every major audio format, supports wireless Dolby Atmos with compatible Samsung TVs, and includes 4K 120Hz HDMI passthrough for people gaming on a PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X. That said, while the bass is strong for a compact subwoofer, it compresses when you push the volume near maximum, so it's not perfect for huge spaces or people who want nightclub-level output. More importantly, if you already own the HW-Q990F or even the older HW-Q990D, upgrading probably will not feel dramatic enough to justify the cost. But for someone starting from TV speakers or an entry-level soundbar, this system can completely change how movies, games, and even sports feel at home.
